As therefore the Blessed, with a burning charity beyond all reckoning, love God, infinitely happy in himself, so with unspeakable joy they behold him, and rejoice most vehemently with him in his beatitude. And as they love him incomparably more than themselves, so they glory incomparably more in his uncreated happiness than in the beatitude bestowed on them; nay, they would rather that they themselves and the whole universe did not exist and were brought to nothing, than that God should for one moment lack or be deprived of his beatitude. Fifth, because of his infinite wisdom. For men naturally desire to see those who excel in wonderful wisdom: how much more delightful, then, to behold in himself him [[Ps 146:5|of his wisdom there is no number|cujus sapientiæ non est finis]] [Denis reads *finis*, 'end', where the Vulgate has *numerus*, 'number']? In this way many other reasons too could be brought forward why it is unspeakably delicious to behold God clearly by sight: for instance, his excellence, boundless and of every kind, in omnipotence, riches, and every wonder, dignity, nobility, fame and glory. Let us therefore cleanse our souls, and prepare them untiringly for so great a beatitude. For [[Matt 5:8|Blessed are the clean of heart: they shall see God|Beati etenim mundo corde, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt]].

paras.t: De qua animarum vestrarum salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ. Sancti enim Prophetæ ex divina revelatione noverunt genus humanum per Christi incarnationem ac passionem esse salvandum: idcirco diligentissime exquisierunt et investigaverunt de ista salute et redemptione tunc fienda, nunc facta per Christum, quo loco et tempore, quo modo et ordine Christus liberaret genus humanum, et animabus fidelium conferret salutem. Exquisierunt autem et investigaverunt de his multipliciter: Primo, rogando Deum ut eis revelaret aliquid de Christi mysteriis. Secundo, quæsierunt illuminationem de his ab angelis sanctis. Tertio, posteriores Prophetæ vel minus illuminati, quæsierunt de his in libris præcedentium Prophetarum, vel ab ore Vatum magis illuminatorum. Hinc etenim Daniel ait: In anno primo Darii, ego Daniel intellexi in libris numerum annorum de quo factus est sermo Dei ad Jeremiam prophetam, etc. Unde et Simeon justus, qui et prophetiæ spiritu splenduit, responsum a Spiritu Sancto legitur accepisse: quia videlicet quotidie exoravit de Christi adventu et tempore ejus certificari. Idcirco responsum est ei, quod ipso adhuc vivente Christus nasceretur, atque ab ipso corporaliter videretur. Sic igitur sancti Prophetæ de Christi mysteriis et salute facta per ipsum, exquisierunt ac prophetaverunt, prout diversis diversa a Deo per angelos revelata fuerunt. Isaias namque de Christi incarnatione, deitate, et suæ Matris virginitate, de Christi quoque miraculis et passione ipsius, de Judæorum excæcatione, gentium illuminatione, evangelicæ legis per totum mundum diffusione, apertissime ac copiosissime prophetavit. David quoque de his omnibus in pluribus psalmis inclyte vaticinatus probatur. De quibus et Jeremias multa prædixit. Daniel vero tempus adventus Christi præ omnibus clarius determinavit ac computavit. Michæas vero de loco nativitatis Christi plenius est locutus.
paras.en: [[1:10|Of which salvation the prophets have inquired and diligently searched|De qua animarum vestrarum salute exquisierunt atque scrutati sunt Prophetæ]]. For the holy Prophets knew by divine revelation that the human race was to be saved through the incarnation and passion of Christ: and so they inquired and searched most diligently into this salvation and redemption, then to be wrought and now wrought by Christ: in what place and at what time, in what manner and order Christ would set the human race free and bestow salvation on the souls of the faithful. And they inquired and searched into these things in many ways. First, by asking God to reveal to them something of the mysteries of Christ. Second, they sought light on these things from the holy angels. Third, the later Prophets, or those less enlightened, sought for these things in the books of the Prophets before them, or from the mouth of seers more enlightened. Hence Daniel says: [[Dan 9:1|In the first year of Darius|In anno primo Darii]], [[Dan 9:2|I, Daniel, understood by books the number of the years, concerning which the word of the Lord came to Jeremias, the prophet|ego Daniel intellexi in libris numerum annorum de quo factus est sermo Dei ad Jeremiam prophetam]], etc. So too Simeon the just[[Luke 2:25||]], who also shone with the spirit of prophecy, is read to have received an answer from the Holy Ghost[[Luke 2:26||]]: because, that is, he prayed every day to be made certain of the coming of Christ and of its time. Therefore the answer was given him that Christ would be born while he was still alive, and would be seen by him in the body. Thus, then, the holy Prophets inquired and prophesied concerning the mysteries of Christ and the salvation wrought by him, according as different things were revealed by God through the angels to different Prophets. For Isaias prophesied most openly and most abundantly of Christ's incarnation, of his Godhead and his Mother's virginity, of Christ's miracles too and of his passion, of the blinding of the Jews, the enlightening of the Gentiles, and the spreading of the law of the Gospel through the whole world. David also is shown to have foretold all these things gloriously in many psalms. Of them Jeremias too foretold much. But Daniel fixed and reckoned the time of Christ's coming more clearly than all the rest[[Dan 9:24||]] [the margin gives Dan. ix, 24–27]. And Michæas spoke more fully of the place of Christ's birth[[Mich 5:2||]].

paras.t: Qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt, id est de magnitudine gratiæ per Christum concessæ fidelibus. Unde apud Joannem habetur: Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est. Propter quod, tempus Christi ac evangelicæ legis, tempus gratiæ appellatur. Hinc ait idem iste Archiapostolus: Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps, annuntiaverunt dies istos. Et sicut idem S. Petrus allegat, Joel propheta de eminentia gratiæ Spiritus Sancti per Christum donata, specialiter prophetavit.
paras.en: [[1:10|who prophesied of the grace to come in you|Qui de futura in vobis gratia prophetaverunt]], that is, of the greatness of the grace granted to the faithful through Christ. Hence we have in John: [[John 1:17|grace and truth came by Jesus Christ|Gratia et veritas per Jesum Christum facta est]]. For this reason the time of Christ and of the law of the Gospel is called the time of grace. Hence this same chief Apostle says: [[Acts 3:24|all the prophets, from Samuel and afterwards|Omnes Prophetæ a Samuel et deinceps]], [[Acts 3:24|have told of these days|annuntiaverunt dies istos]]. And, as St. Peter himself alleges[[Acts 2:16||]], the prophet Joel prophesied in particular of the surpassing grace of the Holy Ghost given through Christ[[Joel 2:28||]] [the margin gives Acts ii, 16–21; Joel ii, 28–32].

paras.t: Scrutantes, non ratione humana, sed illuminatione divina, in quod vel quale tempus significaret in eis spiritus Christi, id est, quo aut quali tempore Spiritus Sanctus revelaret eis adventum Christi esse complendum, an scilicet tempus illud adhuc longe distaret, et an deberet illud tempus esse tempus pacis, an præliorum. Dicitur autem Spiritus Sanctus, spiritus Christi, non solum quia quiescit in eo, sed quoniam vere æternaliterque ab ipso procedit. Quidam tamen per spiritum Christi intelligunt hic spiritum angelicum, seu angelum bonum. Per angelos enim revelationes propheticæ factæ sunt, ut divinus Dionysius docet. Melius tamen per spiritum Christi Spiritus Sanctus accipitur, qui est principalis et primus revelationum prophetalium inspirator, doctor et dator.
paras.en: [[1:11|Searching|Scrutantes]], not by human reason but by divine illumination, [[1:11|what or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ in them did signify|in quod vel quale tempus significaret in eis spiritus Christi]], that is, by what or what kind of time the Holy Ghost would reveal to them that the coming of Christ was to be accomplished: whether, that is, that time was still far off, and whether it was to be a time of peace or of wars. Now the Holy Ghost is called the Spirit of Christ not only because he rests upon him, but because he truly and eternally proceeds from him. Some, however, understand here by the spirit of Christ an angelic spirit, that is, a good angel; for prophetic revelations were made through the angels, as the divine Dionysius teaches. But it is better to take the Spirit of Christ for the Holy Ghost, who is the principal and first inspirer, teacher and giver of prophetic revelations.

paras.t: Porro de isto tempore Christi multa in Prophetis leguntur: ut quum per Aggæum loquitur Deus: Adhuc unum modicum, et ego movebo cœlum et terram, et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus. Per Malachiam quoque: Ecce ego mitto angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam: et statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis. Habacuc quoque ait: Apparebit in finem, et non mentietur; si moram fecerit, exspecta eum, etc. Daniel autem clarissime describit: Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum, etc. Quod vero tempore maximæ pacis Christus nasceretur, per Isaiam et Michæam iisdem pene verbis est prophetatum: Conflabunt, inquiunt, gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces; non levabit gens contra gentem gladium. Unde et in Jeremia habetur: In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter. Quod vero deficiente Judæis rege ac principe propriæ plebis, Christus veniret, Jacob patriarcha in Genesi prædixit: Non auferetur, inquiens, sceptrum de Juda et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium.
paras.en: Many things are read in the Prophets about this time of Christ: as when God speaks by Aggeus: [[Agg 2:7|Yet one little while, and I will move the heaven and the earth|Adhuc unum modicum, et ego movebo cœlum et terram]], [[Agg 2:8|AND THE DESIRED OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME|et veniet Desideratus cunctis gentibus]]. By Malachias too: [[Mal 3:1|Behold I send my angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And presently the Lord, whom you seek, and the angel of the testament, whom you desire, shall come to his temple|Ecce ego mitto angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam: et statim veniet ad templum suum Dominator quem vos quæritis, et Angelus testamenti quem vos vultis]]. Habacuc too says: [[Hab 2:3|it shall appear at the end, and shall not lie: if it make any delay, wait for it|Apparebit in finem, et non mentietur; si moram fecerit, exspecta eum]], etc. And Daniel describes it most clearly: [[Dan 9:24|Seventy weeks are shortened upon thy people|Septuaginta hebdomades abbreviatæ sunt super populum tuum]], etc. That Christ would be born in a time of the greatest peace was prophesied by Isaias and Michæas in almost the same words: [[Is 2:4|they shall turn|Conflabunt]], they say, [[Is 2:4|their swords into ploughshares, and their spears into sickles: nation shall not lift up sword against nation|gladios suos in vomeres, et lanceas suas in falces; non levabit gens contra gentem gladium]][[Mich 4:3||]] [the words are those of Isaias; Michæas has *concident … hastas suas in ligones*]. Hence too we have in Jeremias: [[Jer 23:6|In those days shall Juda be saved, and Israel shall dwell confidently|In diebus illis salvabitur Juda, et Israel habitabit confidenter]] [the margin's reference is partly lost (Jer. xxx…); the same words stand at Jer 33:16, but Denis's *Israel* is the reading of Jer 23:6]. And that Christ would come when the Jews were without a king and prince of their own people, the patriarch Jacob foretold in Genesis: [[Gen 49:10|The sceptre shall not be taken away|Non auferetur]], he says, [[Gen 49:10|from Juda, nor a ruler from his thigh, till he come that is to be sent, and he shall be the expectation of nations|sceptrum de Juda et dux de femore ejus, donec veniat qui mittendus est; et ipse erit exspectatio gentium]].

paras.t: Prænuntians eas quæ in Christo sunt passiones, id est, Spiritus Sanctus fuit Prophetis prædicens quæ et quanta pro hominibus pertulit Christus. Cujus passiones seu pœnas quas toleravit, in Isaia atque in Psalmis luce clarius descriptæ sunt. Prænuntiavit etiam Spiritus Sanctus passiones quæ sunt in Christo, id est persecutiones et pœnas quas Christus in suis sustinet membris, hoc est, quas pro ipso sustinent sui fideles. Et posteriores glorias, id est, Spiritus Sanctus etiam fuit prædicens glorificationes Christi et suorum membrorum: quæ gloriæ passionem Christi secutæ sunt. Nam Christus suæ passionis virtute promeruit sibi ipsi præmium magnum et multiplex accidentale, suis quoque fidelibus meruit glorificationem animarum et corporum. Propter quod ait Apostolus: Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem: propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen. Denique posteriores gloriæ Christi, sunt ejus a morte resurrectio, in cœlum ascensio, suæ majestatis per totum mundum prædicatio, quæ in die Pentecostes fieri cœpit, misso desuper Spiritu Sancto, ejus quoque in die finalis judicii coram omnibus gloriosissima manifestatio. De quibus omnibus prophetaverunt quam plura sancti Prophetæ, ut facile esset monstrare. Sed brevitati studendum est, præsertim quum de his alibi copiosa testimonia sint inducta.
paras.en: [[1:11|when it foretold those sufferings that are in Christ|Prænuntians eas quæ in Christo sunt passiones]], that is, the Holy Ghost foretold to the Prophets what things, and how great, Christ suffered for men. His sufferings, or the pains he bore, are described more clearly than daylight in Isaias[[Is 53:1||]] and in the Psalms[[Ps 21:1||]] [the margin gives Is. liii and Ps. xxi]. The Holy Ghost also foretold the sufferings that are in Christ in this sense: the persecutions and pains which Christ bears in his members, that is, which his faithful bear for him. [[1:11|and the glories that should follow|Et posteriores glorias]]: that is, the Holy Ghost also foretold the glorifyings of Christ and of his members, glories that followed Christ's passion. For by the power of his passion Christ merited for himself a great and manifold accidental reward [that is, a glory added to the essential glory he already had], and merited too for his faithful the glorifying of their souls and bodies. For this reason the Apostle says: [[Phil 2:8|He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death|Humiliavit semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem]]: [[Phil 2:9|For which cause, God also hath exalted him and hath given him a name which is above all names|propter quod et Deus exaltavit illum, et dedit illi nomen quod est super omne nomen]]. Lastly, the glories of Christ that followed are his resurrection from death, his ascension into heaven, the preaching of his majesty through the whole world, which began on the day of Pentecost when the Holy Ghost was sent from on high, and also his most glorious manifestation before all on the day of the last judgment. Of all these the holy Prophets prophesied a great deal, as it would be easy to show. But we must study brevity, especially as abundant testimonies on these things have been brought forward elsewhere.

paras.t: Quibus, puta Prophetis, revelatum est ab Omnipotente, quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem, id est sed vobis, ministrabant, id est ministerialiter atque prophetice prædicebant, ea quæ nunc annuntiata sunt vobis, videlicet mysteria Christi, hoc est tempus, locum et modum suæ incarnationis, nativitatis, passionis, etc. Hæc enim non sunt eorum, sed vestris temporibus adimpleta; nec pro sua, sed pro vestra ad Christum conversione, hæc eis divinitus sunt ostensa. Gratia quoque prophetiæ, quum sit donum gratiæ gratis datæ, ad aliorum ordinatur utilitatem, sicut et cetera hujusmodi dona. Per hoc enim quod ea quæ de Christo prædicaverunt Apostoli, prænunciaverunt Prophetæ, patet veritas fidei christianæ, et multi ad Christum conversi sunt. Hinc in Actibus dixit B. Petrus Judæis, quibus præsentialiter prædicavit: Pœnitentiam agite, et baptizetur unusquisque vestrum, et accipietis donum Spiritus Sancti: vobis enim repromissio hæc, et filiis vestris, et omnibus quoscumque advocaverit Dominus Deus noster. Et rursus: Vos, inquit, estis filii Prophetarum et testamenti quod disposuit ad patres vestros Deus.
paras.en: [[1:12|To whom|Quibus]], that is, to the Prophets, [[1:12|it was revealed|revelatum est]] by the Almighty [[1:12|that, not to themselves but to you|quia non sibi ipsis, vobis autem]] (that is, but to you), [[1:12|they ministered|ministrabant]], that is, foretold as ministers and as prophets, [[1:12|those things which are now declared to you|ea quæ nunc annuntiata sunt vobis]], namely the mysteries of Christ: that is, the time, place and manner of his incarnation, birth, passion, etc. For these were fulfilled not in their times but in yours; and they were shown to them by God not for their own conversion to Christ but for yours. Moreover the grace of prophecy, since it is a gift of grace freely given [Latin *gratia gratis data*: a gift given for the good of others, not to make its holder holy], is ordered to the profit of others, like the other gifts of this kind. For by the fact that the Prophets foretold what the Apostles preached of Christ, the truth of the Christian faith is made plain, and many have been converted to Christ. Hence in the Acts blessed Peter said to the Jews to whom he was preaching in person: [[Acts 2:38|Do penance: and be baptized every one of you|Pœnitentiam agite, et baptizetur unusquisque vestrum]], [[Acts 2:38|And you shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost|et accipietis donum Spiritus Sancti]]: [[Acts 2:39|For the promise is to you and to your children and to all|vobis enim repromissio hæc, et filiis vestris, et omnibus]] [[Acts 2:39|whomsoever the Lord our God shall call|quoscumque advocaverit Dominus Deus noster]]. And again: [[Acts 3:25|You|Vos]], he says, [[Acts 3:25|are the children of the prophets and of the testament which God made to our fathers|estis filii Prophetarum et testamenti quod disposuit ad patres vestros Deus]].

paras.t: Itaque, ista annuntiata sunt vobis annuntiatione certissima, per eos qui evangelizaverunt vobis, videlicet per me ceterosque Apostolos, ac primos Christi discipulos, Spiritu Sancto misso de cœlo, id est eis in die Pentecostes infuso in visibili signo: ita quod non sensu humano, sed Spiritus Sancti instinctu infallibiliter prædicaverunt; in quem, scilicet Spiritum Sanctum, desiderant angeli prospicere: per quod Spiritus Sancti deitas vera insinuatur, quia in eum tanquam in felicitatis suæ objectum, cupiunt angeli intueri. — Sed quum desiderium sit appetitus boni futuri nondum adepti, quomodo angeli, qui Deo sedulo sunt intenti, et eo præsentialissime perfruuntur ac ei uniuntur, dicuntur Spiritus Sancti adspectum desiderare? Et respondendum, quod in desiderio solent duo intelligi. Primum est, appetitio boni futuri. Secundum est, fastidium hujusmodi boni jam diu possessi, vel usque ad saturitatem obtenti. Dicuntur ergo Beati Dei præsentiam et adspectum incessabiliter desiderare, non in quantum desiderium futuri boni appetitum includit, sed prout fastidium omne excludit amor adepti jam boni. Ut enim ait Gregorius: Corporales deliciæ, quum non habentur, grave in se desiderium accendunt; quum autem habentur, protinus per satietatem in fastidium vertunt. Spirituales vero deliciæ, quum non habentur, in fastidio sunt; quum vero habentur, in desiderium. Sicque in eis appetitus saturitatem, atque saturitas appetitum parit. Augent namque spirituales deliciæ desiderium in mente dum satiant.
paras.en: And so these things have been declared to you with a most certain declaration, [[1:12|by them that have preached the gospel to you|per eos qui evangelizaverunt vobis]], namely by me and the other Apostles, and the first disciples of Christ, [[1:12|the Holy Ghost being sent down from heaven|Spiritu Sancto misso de cœlo]], that is, poured into them on the day of Pentecost with a visible sign[[Acts 2:1||]] [the margin gives Acts ii, 1–4]: so that they preached unerringly, not by human understanding but by the prompting of the Holy Ghost; [[1:12|on whom|in quem]], that is, on the Holy Ghost, [[1:12|the angels desire to look|desiderant angeli prospicere]]: by which the true Godhead of the Holy Ghost is intimated, since the angels long to gaze upon him as upon the object of their happiness. But since desire is the appetite for a future good not yet obtained, how are the angels, who are constantly intent on God, enjoy him most immediately present and are united to him, said to desire the sight of the Holy Ghost? The answer is that two things are commonly understood in desire. The first is the seeking of a future good. The second is the absence of weariness [Latin *fastidium*: the distaste that comes of having had enough] with such a good when it has long been possessed or had to the full. The Blessed, then, are said to desire the presence and sight of God unceasingly, not in so far as desire includes the seeking of a future good, but in so far as love of the good already obtained shuts out all weariness. For as Gregory says: Bodily delights, when they are not had, kindle a heavy desire for themselves; but when they are had, they straightway turn through satiety into weariness. Spiritual delights, on the other hand, are wearisome when they are not had; but when they are had, they turn to desire. And so in them appetite begets fulness, and fulness appetite. For spiritual delights increase desire in the mind even as they fill it.

paras.t: Porro quod dicitur, In quem desiderant angeli prospicere, Beda et Glossa exponunt de Christo secundum suam humanitatem: cujus humanitatis tanta est gloria, ut angeli sancti non solum immortalem deitatis essentiam, sed et assumptam Verbi æterni humanitatem gaudeant intueri. Melius tamen istud de Spiritu Sancto exponitur, ita ut summus Apostolus de Spiritu Sancto dicens, In quem desiderant angeli prospicere, denotet immensitatem pietatis divinæ super nos, eo quod Deus Pater Spiritum Sanctum, cujus tanta est majestas ut eum sancti angeli cupiant intueri, misit in terram propter generis humani salutem.
paras.en: The words [[1:12|on whom the angels desire to look|In quem desiderant angeli prospicere]] Bede and the Gloss expound of Christ according to his manhood: whose manhood has so great a glory that the holy angels rejoice to behold not only the immortal essence of the Godhead but also the manhood which the eternal Word assumed. But it is better expounded of the Holy Ghost, so that the chief Apostle, saying of the Holy Ghost, On whom the angels desire to look, points out the boundlessness of God's loving kindness towards us, in that God the Father sent to earth, for the salvation of the human race, the Holy Ghost, whose majesty is so great that the holy angels long to behold him.

paras.t: Circa præhabita scribit Albertus: Omnes Prophetæ de Christo sunt vaticinati. Christus autem consideratur dupliciter: primo, secundum se, ut est caput totius Ecclesiæ; secundo, quantum ad ejus Ecclesiam, quæ dicitur mysticum corpus ipsius. Vaticinium ergo majorum Prophetarum, totum fuit de Christo ut caput est nostrum. Nam vaticinium Isaiæ fuit de ejus incarnatione; vaticinium Jeremiæ, de ejus passione; vaticinium Ezechielis, de ejus resurrectione; vaticinium Danielis, de ipsius ascensione. Prophetæ vero minores vaticinati sunt de corpore ejus mystico, quod est Ecclesia. Ideo dicti sunt Prophetæ minores, quia de mystico corpore Christi, et non de Christo capite prophetaverunt.
paras.en: On what has been said, Albert writes: All the Prophets foretold Christ. But Christ is considered in two ways: first, in himself, as he is head of the whole Church[[Eph 5:23||]]; second, as regards his Church, which is called his mystical body. The prophecy of the major Prophets, then, was wholly of Christ as he is our head. For the prophecy of Isaias was of his incarnation; that of Jeremias, of his passion; that of Ezechiel, of his resurrection; that of Daniel, of his ascension. But the minor Prophets prophesied of his mystical body, which is the Church. They are called minor Prophets for this reason, that they prophesied of the mystical body of Christ and not of Christ the head.

paras.t: Sed miror quod tantus doctor, tamque subtilis expositor, dicit hæc: quæ stare non valent, nisi forsitan valde pie extenuentur. In primis ergo quod ait, quod totum vaticinium majorum Prophetarum fuit de Christo ut est caput nostrum, duplicem habet instantiam: Priorem, quia de Judæorum, Chaldæorum, Philistæorum, Moabitarum, Ammonitarum, Ægyptiorum, aliarumque gentium diversarum excessibus, punitionibus, reparationibus multa prædixerunt Prophetæ. Posteriorem, quia de mystico Christi corpore, utpote Ecclesia, copiose prophetarunt. Unde, secundum Hieronymum, universa Christi atque Ecclesiæ mysteria tam diffuse Isaias descripsit, ut non tam propheta quam evangelista dicendus sit. Apostolus quoque Paulus in epistola ad Romanos multa allegat ex Isaia de Ecclesia ex gentilitate collecta. Insuper ad Galatas allegat ex Isaia de ipsa Ecclesia: Lætare, sterilis quæ non paris; erumpe et clama, quæ non parturis. Quæ verba apud Isaiam secundum antiquam translationem habentur. Præterea, ultimam visionem Ezechielis de templo difficillimam atque longissimam, Hieronymus, Gregorius aliique doctores communiter exponunt de Christi Ecclesia. — Quod autem secundo ait Albertus, vaticinium Isaiæ esse de Christi incarnatione, Jeremiæ de ejus passione, Ezechielis de ejus resurrectione, Danielis de ejus ascensione, nec præcise nec appropriate videtur posse salvari, quoniam Isaias multo diffusius vaticinatus est de Christi passione quam Jeremias, ut patet in locis multis Isaiæ. Et quod Albertus ex Ezechiele allegat de Christi resurrectione, videlicet de accessione ossium ad ossa, de Christi resurrectione nequaquam ad litteram dictum est, nec verificatur de ea, quoniam corpus Christi non fuit dissolutum, nec caro ejus vidit corruptionem, ut in Actibus docet ac probat princeps Apostolorum. Multa hujusmodi possent contra hæc verba Alberti induci. — Quod demum tertio ait, minores Prophetas non prophetasse de corpore Christi vero, seu capite Christo, sed solum de corpore mystico, prorsus nil valet, nec canonicis concordat Scripturis: quum et Matthæus evangelista alleget ad litteram illud Michææ: Et tu, Bethlehem terra Juda, etc. Eodem quoque capitulo allegat S. Matthæus illud Osee: Ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum. Amplius, per Zachariam de Christo ad litteram, apertissime est prædictum: Exulta satis, filia Sion, ecce rex tuus venit tibi, etc., quod in Matthæo et Joanne allegatur de Christo. Iterum, de Christi resurrectione prædictum est per Sophoniam et Osee. Paulus quoque apostolus ad Romanos de Ecclesia inducit illud Osee: Et erit in loco ubi dicitur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis. Et rursus illud Osee: Vocabo non plebem meam, plebem meam. Adhuc etiam de Christi adventu, et præsentatione ejus in templo, apud Aggæum et Malachiam evidenter legitur prophetatum. — Postremo, cur duodecim Prophetæ dicantur minores Prophetæ, dictum est alio loco. Nec enim illa est ratio quam assignat Albertus. Imo, si rite pensetur, Zacharias de Prophetis minoribus unus, diffusius ac evidentius ad litteram vaticinatur de Christo, quam Ezechiel Prophetarum unus majorum.
paras.en: But I wonder that so great a doctor and so subtle an expositor says these things, which cannot stand unless perhaps they are softened down very charitably. First, then, what he says, that the whole prophecy of the major Prophets was of Christ as he is our head, meets a twofold objection. The first, that the Prophets foretold many things of the excesses, punishments and restorations of the Jews, the Chaldeans, the Philistines, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Egyptians and various other nations. The second, that they prophesied abundantly of the mystical body of Christ, namely the Church. Hence, according to Jerome, Isaias described all the mysteries of Christ and of the Church so fully that he should be called not so much a prophet as an evangelist. The apostle Paul too, in the epistle to the Romans, alleges many things from Isaias about the Church gathered from among the Gentiles[[Rom 9:27||]][[Rom 10:15||]][[Rom 10:16||]][[Rom 10:20||]] [the margin gives Rom. ix, 27–29; x, 15, 16, 20, etc.]. Moreover, to the Galatians he alleges from Isaias of the Church itself: [[Gal 4:27|Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not: break forth and cry thou that travailest not|Lætare, sterilis quæ non paris; erumpe et clama, quæ non parturis]][[Is 54:1||]]. These words are found in Isaias according to the old translation [the Vulgate of Is 54:1 reads *Lauda, sterilis*, ‘Give praise, O thou barren’]. Besides, the last vision of Ezechiel, of the temple[[Ezech 40:1||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xl–xlviii], most difficult and very long, is commonly expounded by Jerome, Gregory and the other doctors of the Church of Christ. Again, what Albert says in the second place, that the prophecy of Isaias is of Christ's incarnation, that of Jeremias of his passion, that of Ezechiel of his resurrection, and that of Daniel of his ascension, it seems, cannot be upheld either strictly or fittingly, since Isaias prophesied much more fully of Christ's passion than Jeremias, as is plain in many places of Isaias. And what Albert alleges from Ezechiel about Christ's resurrection, namely about the coming together of bone to bone[[Ezech 37:7||]] [the margin gives Ezech. xxxvii], was in no way said literally of Christ's resurrection, nor is it verified of it, since the body of Christ was not dissolved, [[Acts 2:31|neither did his flesh see corruption|nec caro ejus vidit corruptionem]], as the prince of the Apostles teaches and proves in the Acts. Many things of this kind could be brought against these words of Albert. Lastly, what he says in the third place, that the minor Prophets did not prophesy of the true body of Christ, or of Christ the head, but only of the mystical body, is worth nothing at all and does not agree with the canonical Scriptures: for Matthew the evangelist alleges according to the letter that saying of Michæas: [[Matt 2:6|And thou Bethlehem the land of Juda|Et tu, Bethlehem terra Juda]], etc.[[Mich 5:2||]] In the same chapter too St. Matthew alleges that saying of Osee: [[Matt 2:15|Out of Egypt have I called my son|Ex Ægypto vocavi filium meum]][[Osee 11:1||]]. Further, it was foretold of Christ according to the letter, most openly, by Zacharias: [[Zach 9:9|Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Sion|Exulta satis, filia Sion]], [[Zach 9:9|BEHOLD THY KING will come to thee|ecce rex tuus venit tibi]], etc., which is alleged of Christ in Matthew and John. Again, Christ's resurrection was foretold by Sophonias and Osee. The apostle Paul too, to the Romans, brings in of the Church that saying of Osee: [[Osee 1:10|And it shall be in the place where it shall be said to them: You are not my people: it shall be said to them: Ye are the sons of the living God|Et erit in loco ubi dicitur eis, Non populus meus vos; dicetur eis, Filii Dei viventis]] [the margin gives Rom. ix, 25; Paul quotes this at Rom 9:26, but Denis gives the words of Osee 1:10]. And again that saying of Osee: [[Rom 9:25|I will call that which was not my people, my people|Vocabo non plebem meam, plebem meam]]. Further still, Christ's coming and his presentation in the temple are plainly read to have been prophesied in Aggeus and Malachias[[Agg 2:8||]][[Mal 3:1||]]. Lastly, why the twelve Prophets are called minor Prophets has been said in another place; for that is not the reason Albert assigns. Indeed, if it is rightly weighed, Zacharias, who is one of the minor Prophets, prophesies of Christ according to the letter more fully and more plainly than Ezechiel, who is one of the major Prophets.

paras.t: Consequenter princeps Apostolorum hortatur fideles, ne gratiam sibi divinitus oblatam parvi pendant aut negligant, sed ea se dignos exhibeant. Propter quod, id est, quia Prophetæ non sibi, sed vobis annuntiaverunt de Christo, succincti lumbos mentis vestræ. Lumbi carnis, in quibus viget luxuria, partes sunt corporis. Lumbi mentis sunt: intellectus, qui generat verbum; et voluntas, quæ parit amorem. Lumbos ergo mentis accingere, est intellectum a vanarum cogitationum fluxu, a distractionibus erroribusque reprimere, et eum in captivitatem redigere in Christi obsequium, ut subjectus sit fidei; voluntatem quoque ab inordinatis desideriis coarctare. Lumbos autem carnis accingere, est carnalia desideria et eorum carnales fœditates domare. Hinc ait et Christus: Sint lumbi vestri præcincti; et Paulus ad Ephesios, State, inquit, succincti lumbos vestros in veritate.
paras.en: Next the prince of the Apostles exhorts the faithful not to think little of, or neglect, the grace offered them by God, but to show themselves worthy of it. [[1:13|Wherefore|Propter quod]], that is, because the Prophets announced Christ not to themselves but to you, [[1:13|having the loins of your mind girt up|succincti lumbos mentis vestræ]]. The loins of the flesh, in which lust is strong, are parts of the body. The loins of the mind are the understanding, which begets the word, and the will, which brings forth love. To gird the loins of the mind, then, is to hold back the understanding from the stream of vain thoughts, from distractions and errors, and so, [[2 Cor 10:5|bringing into captivity every understanding unto the obedience of Christ|in captivitatem redigere in Christi obsequium]], to make it subject to faith; and also to restrain the will from disordered desires. But to gird the loins of the flesh is to tame carnal desires and their carnal foulnesses. Hence Christ too says: [[Luke 12:35|Let your loins be girt|Sint lumbi vestri præcincti]]; and Paul to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:14|Stand|State]], he says, [[Eph 6:14|having your loins girt about with truth|succincti lumbos vestros in veritate]].

paras.t: Itaque, Succincti lumbos mentis vestræ, id est, rationem et voluntatem reformatas habentes: quatenus juxta Pauli doctrinam, Non simus parvuli fluctuantes, nec circumferamur omni vento doctrinæ; sobrii, moderantiam in cibo et potu servantes: quemadmodum jubet Salvator, Attendite vobis, ne graventur corda vestra crapula vel ebrietate; et perfecti, non solum amicos in Deo, sed et inimicos propter Deum sincere diligendo, eisque bona pro malis reddendo: prout in Matthæo loquitur Christus, Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est. Vel, Perfecti, non solum præcepta, sed evangelica quoque consilia adimplendo: juxta quod et Veritas ait, Si vis perfectus esse, vade et vende omnia quæ habes, et da pauperibus, et sequere me. Multi autem sunt gradus perfectionis. Sperate in eam quæ offertur vobis gratiam: id est, dona gratiæ, quæ Christus in vita hac offert vobis, omnes ad pœnitentiam et profectum hortando, dona quoque gloriæ (quæ est gratia consummata, juxta illud apostoli Pauli, Gratia Dei vita æterna), constanter confidite adipisci, eaque obtinere satagite. Unde et Paulus disseruit: Hortamur vos ne in vacuum gratiam Dei recipiatis; et rursus, Quomodo effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem? Porro, spes quum sit theologica virtus, directe et immediate habet Deum pro objecto; secundario vero respicit ea per quæ ad summum bonum perducimur et juvamur.
paras.en: So then, [[1:13|having the loins of your mind girt up|Succincti lumbos mentis vestræ]], that is, having your reason and will reformed: so that, according to Paul's teaching, [[Eph 4:14|we be no more children tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine|Non simus parvuli fluctuantes, nec circumferamur omni vento doctrinæ]]; [[1:13|being sober|sobrii]], keeping moderation in food and drink, as the Saviour commands: [[Luke 21:34|take heed to yourselves, lest perhaps your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting and drunkenness|Attendite vobis, ne graventur corda vestra crapula vel ebrietate]]; [[1:13|perfectly|et perfecti]] [Denis reads *et perfecti*, ‘and perfect’, where the Vulgate has *perfecte*, ‘perfectly’], that is, perfect by loving sincerely not only friends in God but also enemies for God's sake, and returning them good for evil, as Christ says in Matthew: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote perfecti, sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]]. Or, perfect by fulfilling not only the precepts but also the counsels of the Gospel, according to what the Truth also says: [[Matt 19:21|If thou wilt be perfect, go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor|Si vis perfectus esse, vade et vende omnia quæ habes, et da pauperibus]], [[Matt 19:21|follow me|sequere me]]. And there are many degrees of perfection. [[1:13|trust|Sperate]] [[1:13|in the grace which is offered you|in eam quæ offertur vobis gratiam]]: that is, the gifts of grace which Christ offers you in this life, exhorting all to penance and to progress, and also the gifts of glory (which is grace made complete, according to that of the apostle Paul, [[Rom 6:23|the grace of God, life everlasting|Gratia Dei vita æterna]]): trust steadfastly that you will obtain them, and strive to gain them. Hence Paul too taught: [[2 Cor 6:1|do exhort you that you receive not the grace of God in vain|Hortamur vos ne in vacuum gratiam Dei recipiatis]]; and again, [[Heb 2:3|How shall we escape if we neglect so great salvation?|Quomodo effugiemus, si tantam neglexerimus salutem?]] Now hope, since it is a theological virtue, has God directly and immediately for its object; but secondarily it looks to those things by which we are led and helped to the supreme good.

paras.t: Sperate ergo in gratiam istam, et eam adipisci confidite in revelatione Jesu Christi, id est in manifesta ipsius declaratione, quum se vobis ostenderit intuendum sicuti est: in qua ostensione, gratia consummata seu salus vestra consistit. Unde apud Joannem Christus hanc sui manifestationem promittit pro præmio, dicens: Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo; et ego diligam eum, et manifestabo ei me ipsum. Denique, quia plenaria salus in corpore et anima in die judicii tribuetur, potest quod dictum est, In revelatione Jesu Christi, referri ad nativitatem, item manifestam apparitionem Christi in die judicii, quando illud Isaiæ implebitur: Revelabitur gloria Domini, et videbit omnis caro salutare Dei nostri.
paras.en: Trust, then, in this grace, and be confident that you will obtain it [[1:13|in the revelation of Jesus Christ|in revelatione Jesu Christi]], that is, in his open showing of himself, when he shows himself to you to be beheld [[1 John 3:2|as he is|sicuti est]]: in which showing your completed grace, that is, your salvation, consists. Hence in John Christ promises this manifestation of himself as a reward, saying: [[John 14:21|he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father: and I will love him and will manifest myself to him|Qui diligit me, diligetur a Patre meo; et ego diligam eum, et manifestabo ei me ipsum]]. Lastly, since full salvation in body and soul will be given on the day of judgment, the words, In the revelation of Jesus Christ, can be referred to the nativity, and also to the open appearing of Christ on the day of judgment, when that saying of Isaias will be fulfilled: [[Is 40:5|the glory of the Lord shall be revealed|Revelabitur gloria Domini]], [[Is 40:5|and all flesh together shall see|et videbit omnis caro]] the salvation of our God [these last words, *salutare Dei nostri*, are not in the Vulgate of Is 40:5; they stand at Is 52:10 and Luke 3:6].

paras.t: Quasi filii obedientiæ, id est Deo et vestris prælatis humiliter subditi. Obedientia quippe omnem Christi fidelem maxime decet, quum ipsemet Christus testetur: Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me; itemque, Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio. Imo factus est obediens Patri usque ad mortem. Idcirco inobedientiæ filii, non Christi, sed diaboli sunt ministri. Porro hæc dictio, Quasi, notat hic veritatem, non similitudinem tantum. Non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ desideriis, id est, non rursus conformantes vos ipsos vitiosis atque carnalibus affectibus, in quibus tempore vestræ infidelitatis fuistis. Omnes autem inordinati et pravi affectus, dici possunt desideria ignorantiæ, quia ex ignorantia quadam nascuntur, eo modo quo, juxta Philosophum, omnis peccans est ignorans: quoniam male judicat saltem in particulari, quamvis in generali veritatem agnoscat. Quum enim, divino Dionysio testante, nullus respiciens ad malum operetur, quia videlicet malum sub ratione mali non appetitur, quum bonum sit appetitus objectum: constat quod omnis qui peccat, malum sub ratione boni apparentis apprehendat, sive admittat; sicque ignorans et cæcus est, atque ex rationis ignorantia, inadvertentia, defectu, aut errore contingit quod peccat, quod affectionem suam non rectificat, quod inordinationem et carnalitatem non reprimit. Idcirco in Proverbiis dicitur: Via stulti recta in oculis ejus. Et denuo Salomon loquitur: Stultis illudit peccatum. Et iterum dictum est: Qui peccat, insipiens est et indoctus.
paras.en: [[1:14|As children of obedience|Quasi filii obedientiæ]], that is, humbly subject to God and to your prelates. For obedience above all befits every one of Christ's faithful, since Christ himself testifies: [[John 6:38|I came down from heaven, not to do my own will but the will of him that sent me|Descendi de cœlo, non ut faciam voluntatem meam, sed voluntatem ejus qui misit me]]; and also, [[John 14:31|as the Father hath given me commandments, so do I|Sicut mandatum dedit mihi Pater, sic facio]]. Nay, he was [[Phil 2:8|becoming obedient|factus est obediens]] to the Father [[Phil 2:8|unto death|usque ad mortem]]. Therefore the children of disobedience are ministers not of Christ but of the devil. Now this word *as* here denotes the truth, not merely a likeness. [[1:14|not fashioned according to the former desires of your ignorance|Non configurati prioribus ignorantiæ vestræ desideriis]]: that is, not conforming yourselves again to the vicious and carnal affections in which you lived in the time of your unbelief. Now all disordered and wicked affections can be called desires of ignorance, because they arise from a kind of ignorance, in the way in which, according to the Philosopher, every sinner is ignorant: for he judges wrongly at least in the particular case, though in general he acknowledges the truth. For since, as the divine Dionysius testifies, no one acts with his eye on evil, because evil is not sought under the aspect of evil, since the good is the object of the appetite, it is plain that everyone who sins grasps or takes up evil under the aspect of an apparent good; and so he is ignorant and blind, and it is from ignorance, inattention, failure or error of reason that he sins, that he does not set his affection right, that he does not check its disorder and carnality. Therefore it is said in Proverbs: [[Prov 12:15|The way of a fool is right in his own eyes|Via stulti recta in oculis ejus]]. And again Solomon says: [[Prov 14:9|A fool will laugh at sin|Stultis illudit peccatum]] [Denis reads *Stultis illudit peccatum*, ‘sin mocks fools’; the Vulgate has *Stultus illudet peccatum*]. And again it has been said: He that sins is foolish and unlearned.

paras.t: Sed secundum eum qui vocavit vos Sanctum, et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis: id est, quemadmodum Deus qui per gratiam suam ad evangelicæ legis veritatem perduxit vos, in se ipso purus et virtuosus consistit, atque in omni operatione sua recte et sapienter se habet; ita et vos pro modulo vestro, mundi et virtuosi sitis in tota vita vestra. Scriptum est enim in Levitico: Sancti eritis, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Sic namque in Levitico loquitur Deus: Nolite contaminare animas vestras: ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester; sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum. Denique aliqua in Scripturis traduntur, non per modum præcepti, et tamen præcepta sunt, ut quum Deus ait per Moysen: Non adorabis deos alienos, nec servies eis. Et tale est istud quod dicitur hic, Sancti eritis, loquendo de sanctitate secundum aliquem gradum. Sanctum quippe in una significatione, est idem quod firmum: et unusquisque fidelis tenetur esse in fide, spe et caritate tam firmus, ut proponat, pro nulla re mundi se a Deo per mortale peccatum avertere, aut contra fidem, spem, caritatemve agere. Idcirco in Ecclesiastico præcipitur: Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui. Paulus quoque Corinthiis scribens: Stabiles, inquit, estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper. Rursus, sanctum est idem quod purum: et unusquisque tenetur ab omni mortali peccato esse immunis. Sicque oravit Propheta: Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum. Proprie autem et communi modo loquendi, sanctus vocatur, qui in caritate et omni virtute perfectus est, utpote vir heroicus et divinus, ad plenam passionum reformationem provectus: et ita non tenetur quilibet esse sanctus.
paras.en: [[1:15|But according to him that hath called you, who is holy|Sed secundum eum qui vocavit vos Sanctum]], [[1:15|be you also in all manner of conversation holy|et ipsi sancti in omni conversatione sitis]]: that is, as God, who by his grace has brought you to the truth of the law of the Gospel, is pure and virtuous in himself, and in all his working acts rightly and wisely, so you also, in your small measure, be clean and virtuous in your whole life. [[1:16|Because it is written|Scriptum est enim]] in Leviticus: [[1:16|You shall be holy, for I am holy|Sancti eritis, quoniam ego sanctus sum]]. For thus God speaks in Leviticus: [[Lev 11:44|Defile not your souls|Nolite contaminare animas vestras]]: [[Lev 11:44|For I am the Lord your God. Be holy because I am holy|ego enim sum Dominus Deus vester; sancti estote, quoniam ego sanctus sum]]. Moreover, some things are delivered in the Scriptures not in the form of a precept, and yet they are precepts: as when God says by Moses: [[Ex 20:5|Thou shalt not adore|Non adorabis]] [[Ex 20:3|strange gods|deos alienos]], [[Ex 20:5|nor serve them|nec servies eis]]. And of this kind is what is said here, [[1:16|You shall be holy|Sancti eritis]], speaking of holiness in some degree. For *holy* in one meaning is the same as *firm*: and every one of the faithful is bound to be so firm in faith, hope and charity that he purposes, for nothing in the world, to turn away from God by mortal sin, or to act against faith, hope or charity. Therefore it is commanded in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 5:12|Be steadfast in the way of the Lord, and in the truth of thy judgment|Esto firmus in via Domini, et in veritate sensus tui]]. Paul too, writing to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 15:58|be ye steadfast|Stabiles]], he says, [[1 Cor 15:58|and unmoveable: always abounding in the work of the Lord|estote et immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper]]. Again, *holy* is the same as *pure*: and everyone is bound to be free from all mortal sin. So the Prophet prayed: [[Ps 85:2|Preserve my soul, for I am holy|Custodi animam meam, quoniam sanctus sum]]. But properly, and in the common way of speaking, he is called holy who is perfect in charity and in every virtue, a heroic and godlike man, as it were, advanced to the full reform of the passions: and in this sense not everyone is bound to be holy.

paras.t: Præcepit ergo piissimus Deus, ut sicut ipse est sanctus, sic servi sui sint sancti. Nam sancti sapientesque domini, servos volunt habere honestos, probos, prudentes, prout eorum excellentiam decet. Denique ad hoc Filius Dei venit in mundum, ut sine timore de manu inimicorum nostrorum liberati, serviamus illi in sanctitate et justitia coram ipso omnibus diebus nostris, ut apud Lucam asseritur. Iterum, quia ad imaginem et similitudinem suam nos condidit Deus, requirit ut ei virtutibus assimilemur, præsertim quum ipse velit a nobis pater vocari: pater autem vult ut filii sui suas sequantur virtutes. Et hæc est ingens ac præclarissima dignitas rationalis creaturæ, suo Creatori sic conformari. Propter quod væ eis qui per vitam suam carnalem bestiis conformantur. Et gravius væ eis qui per malitiam, crudelitatem, nequitiam, ac impiam conversationem assimilantur dæmonibus. Deo igitur in pietate, caritate, justitia et sanctitate pro viribus assimilari conemur, sicut et Paulus hortatur: Imitatores Dei estote, sicut filii carissimi. Unde et Christus: Estote, ait, misericordes, sicut et Pater vester misericors est; itemque, Estote perfecti, sicut Pater cœlestis. Hinc et in Deuteronomio locutus est Moyses: Perfectus eris et absque macula cum Domino Deo tuo.
paras.en: The most loving God, then, commanded that as he himself is holy, so his servants should be holy. For holy and wise masters want to have servants who are upright, good and prudent, as befits their own excellence. Moreover the Son of God came into the world for this, [[Luke 1:74|That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, we may serve him without fear|ut sine timore de manu inimicorum nostrorum liberati, serviamus illi]] [[Luke 1:75|In holiness and justice before him, all our days|in sanctitate et justitia coram ipso omnibus diebus nostris]], as is declared in Luke. Again, because God made us to his image and likeness[[Gen 1:26||]][[Gen 1:27||]], he requires that we be made like him in virtues, especially as he wills to be called father by us: and a father wants his children to follow his virtues. And this is the vast and most glorious dignity of the rational creature, to be thus conformed to its Creator. For this reason woe to those who by their carnal life are conformed to the beasts; and a heavier woe to those who by malice, cruelty, wickedness and an impious way of life are made like the devils. Let us therefore strive with all our strength to be made like God in loving kindness, charity, justice and holiness, as Paul too exhorts: [[Eph 5:1|Be ye therefore followers of God, as most dear children|Imitatores Dei estote, sicut filii carissimi]]. Hence Christ too: [[Luke 6:36|Be ye|Estote]], he says, [[Luke 6:36|therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful|misericordes, sicut et Pater vester misericors est]]; and also, [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father|Estote perfecti, sicut Pater cœlestis]]. Hence in Deuteronomy too Moses spoke: [[Deut 18:13|Thou shalt be perfect, and without spot before the Lord thy God|Perfectus eris et absque macula cum Domino Deo tuo]].

paras.t: Præterea quæri potest, quomodo intelligenda sint aut fieri possint ista, quum apud Isaiam dicatur: Facti sumus ut immundi omnes nos; quasi pannus menstruatæ universæ justitiæ nostræ. Primus quoque ille apostata cecidit, quia dixit: Similis ero Altissimo. Et respondendum, quod comparatione divinæ justitiæ, dicitur nostræ justitiæ similes panno menstruatæ: quia in multis offendimus omnes, et multæ defectuositates ac culpæ nostris bonis actibus admiscentur. Imo respectu puritatis et perfectionis ac sapientiæ Creatoris æterni, omnis puritas, perfectio, sapientia nostra nullius momenti est, et tanquam immunditia, imperfectio et insipientia reputatur, quemadmodum in Jeremia legitur: Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua. Unde et in libro Job fertur: Quid est homo, ut immaculatus sit, et justus appareat natus de muliere? Ecce inter Sanctos ejus nemo immutabilis, et cœli non sunt munda in conspectu ejus. Et rursus sanctus Job protestatur: Non justificatur homo compositus Deo. Ideo orat Propheta: Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo, Domine, quia non justificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivens. Postremo, sanctitas nostra differt ac deficit a sanctitate Dei in multis et infinite, quum Deus sit essentialiter, independenter, invariabiliter, incircumscriptibiliter sanctus. Ut autem, juxta intentionem Scripturæ, sancti simus in omni conversatione, non solum requiritur ut mortalia declinemus peccata, sed venialia etiam cum diligentia vitare oportet, et semper coram Deo timoratum ac custoditum consistere, quum in Ecclesiastico scriptum sit: Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua; et in Proverbiis, Omni custodia custodi cor tuum.
paras.en: It may further be asked how these things are to be understood, or how they can be done, since it is said in Isaias: [[Is 64:6|we are all become as one unclean, and all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|Facti sumus ut immundi omnes nos; quasi pannus menstruatæ universæ justitiæ nostræ]]. And that first apostate fell because he said: [[Is 14:14|I will be like the most High|Similis ero Altissimo]]. The answer is that it is in comparison with God's justice that our justices are said to be like the rag of a menstruous woman: because [[Jas 3:2|in many things we all offend|in multis offendimus omnes]], and many failings and faults are mixed with our good acts. Indeed, in respect of the purity and perfection and wisdom of the eternal Creator, all our purity, perfection and wisdom is of no account, and is reckoned as uncleanness, imperfection and folly, as we read in Jeremias: [[Jer 10:14|Every man is become a fool for knowledge|Stultus factus est omnis homo a scientia sua]]. Hence it is said in the book of Job too: [[Job 15:14|What is man that he should be without spot, and he that is born of a woman that he should appear just?|Quid est homo, ut immaculatus sit, et justus appareat natus de muliere?]] [[Job 15:15|Behold among his saints none is unchangeable, and the heavens are not pure in his sight|Ecce inter Sanctos ejus nemo immutabilis, et cœli non sunt munda in conspectu ejus]]. And again holy Job declares: [[Job 9:2|man cannot be justified, compared with God|Non justificatur homo compositus Deo]]. Therefore the Prophet prays: [[Ps 142:2|enter not into judgment with thy servant|Non intres in judicium cum servo tuo]], O Lord, [[Ps 142:2|for in thy sight no man living shall be justified|quia non justificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivens]] [the margin gives Ps. cxliii, 2]. Lastly, our holiness differs from and falls short of the holiness of God in many ways and infinitely, since God is holy essentially, independently, unchangeably and without limit. But that we may be holy in all manner of conversation, according to the intention of Scripture, it is required not only that we shun mortal sins: we must also avoid venial ones with diligence, and stand always before God fearful and watchful, since it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 27:4|Unless thou hold thyself diligently in the fear of the Lord, thy house shall quickly be overthrown|Si non in timore Domini tenueris te instanter, cito subvertetur domus tua]]; and in Proverbs: [[Prov 4:23|With all watchfulness keep thy heart|Omni custodia custodi cor tuum]].

1.title: ELUCIDATIO RESIDUÆ PARTIS HUJUS PRIMI CAPITULI, AB EO LOCO QUO DICITUR : ET SI PATREM INVOCATIS EUM.
1.title_en: Elucidation of the remaining part of this first chapter, from the place where it is said: And if you invoke as Father him

paras.t: Quoniam Salomone testante, timor Dei est fons vitæ, consequenter hortatur gloriosissimus apostolici chori hierarcha, sanctissimus Petrus, ut Deum filialiter timeamus. Et si, pro quia, patrem invocatis, id est, orando patrem nominatis, eum qui sine acceptione personarum judicat secundum uniuscujusque opus, id est, quemlibet judicat secundum opera sua : intelligendo per opera, etiam actus interiores, et locutiones, debitorumque actuum omissiones. Unde apud Job inducitur : Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas : opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet. Et Jeremias ait : Domine Deus fortissime, cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas. Qualiter autem personarum acceptio non competat Deo, et quid sit personarum acceptio, et de peccato ipsius, dictum est supra in expositione secundi capituli epistolæ Jacobi. In timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini, id est, tempore quo in hoc sæculo subsistitis, vivite in Dei timore filiali, ne tanto patre sitis indigni, et ne in sui judicii incidatis rigorem, propter vestram ignaviam ac periculosam securitatem : ne judicem districtum aliquando sentiatis, quem nunc pium patrem contemnitis, et timere ac honorare recusatis. Qui enim sine timore est, justificari non potest. Et Christus in Evangelio jubet : Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam.
paras.en: Since, as Solomon testifies, the fear of God is a fountain of life[[Prov 14:27||]], the most glorious hierarch of the apostolic choir, most holy Peter, next exhorts us to fear God as sons. [[1:17|And if|Et si]], that is, since, [[1:17|you invoke as Father|patrem invocatis]], that is, name him Father in praying, [[1:17|him who, without respect of persons, judgeth according to every one's work|eum qui sine acceptione personarum judicat secundum uniuscujusque opus]], that is, judges each according to his works: understanding by works also interior acts, and speech, and the omission of acts that were due. Hence in Job it is said: [[Job 34:10|far from God be wickedness, and iniquity from|Absit a Deo impietas, et ab Omnipotente iniquitas]]: [[Job 34:11|For he will render to a man his work, and according to the ways of every one|opus enim hominis reddet ei, et juxta vias singulorum restituet]]. And Jeremias says: [[Jer 32:18|O most mighty|Domine Deus fortissime]], [[Jer 32:19|whose eyes are open upon all the ways of the children of Adam, to render unto every one according to his ways|cujus oculi aperti sunt super omnes filios Adam, ut reddas unicuique secundum vias suas]]. How respect of persons does not befit God, what respect of persons is, and of its sin, has been said above in the exposition of the second chapter of the epistle of James[[Jas 2:1||]][[Jas 2:9||]]. [[1:17|converse in fear during the time of your sojourning here|In timore incolatus vestri tempore conversamini]], that is, in the time in which you abide in this world, live in the filial fear of God, lest you be unworthy of so great a Father, and lest you fall into the rigour of his judgment through your sloth and perilous security: lest one day you feel as a strict judge him whom now you despise as a loving Father, and refuse to fear and honour. For he that is without fear cannot be justified[[Ecclus 1:28||]]. And Christ commands in the Gospel: [[Matt 10:28|fear him that can destroy both soul and body in hell|Eum timete, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam perdere in gehennam]].

paras.t: Sed instare quis potest, quia non videtur adaptatio ista Petri apostoli convenire adaptationi qua apud Malachiam loquitur Deus : Filius honorat patrem, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? et si dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus? Ex quibus verbis elicitur, quod Deo debetur timor, in quantum est dominus, et honor, in quantum est pater. Quomodo ergo nunc ait Apostolus, Si patrem invocatis Deum, in timore conversamini? Videtur enim debuisse dixisse, Si dominum invocatis, etc. — Et respondendum, quod Deo debetur timor castus, sanctus et filialis, in quantum est pater, quia hic timor ex magnitudine oritur caritatis. Timor vero servilis aut initialis impenditur Deo, ut domino. Est autem timor filialis, quo vitatur malum culpæ ne Deus pater offendatur aut inhonoretur. Sicque timor filialis realiter est fuga seu abominatio culpæ. De quo in Ecclesiastico multa scribuntur, videlicet : Timor Domini super omnia se superposuit. Beatus cui datum est habere timorem Dei. Timor Domini sicut paradisus benedictionis. Est autem timor Dei omni Christiano præcipue necessarius, quia præservat a vitiis, custodit in bonis, et sollicitum facit timentem, ne cadat in laqueos inimici. Iterum, semper coram Deo solliciti esse debemus ac pavidi, quia nescimus an digni simus amore vel odio, hoc est, an simus in caritate et gratia, an non : et rursus, quoniam ignoramus quid finaliter erit nobis, an scilicet sempiterna damnatio, an salus perpetua; et quia ad omne malum sumus tam proni, atque in laqueorum medio ambulamus.
paras.en: But someone may object that this adaptation of the apostle Peter does not seem to agree with that by which God speaks in Malachias: [[Mal 1:6|The son honoureth the father, and the servant his master: if then I be a father, where is my honour? and if I be a master, where is my fear|Filius honorat patrem, et servus timet dominum suum. Si ergo pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? et si dominus ego sum, ubi est timor meus?]]? From these words it is drawn that fear is owed to God inasmuch as he is Lord, and honour inasmuch as he is Father. How then does the Apostle now say: If you invoke God as Father, converse in fear? He seems to have ought to say: If you invoke him as Lord, etc. — And it must be answered that chaste, holy and filial fear is owed to God inasmuch as he is Father, for this fear arises from the greatness of charity. But servile or initial fear [that is, the fear of punishment, and the beginner's fear mixed of love and dread of punishment] is paid to God as Lord. Filial fear is that by which the evil of fault is shunned lest God the Father be offended or dishonoured. And thus filial fear is really a flight from, or abhorrence of, fault. Of it much is written in Ecclesiasticus, namely: [[Ecclus 25:14|The fear of God hath set itself above all things|Timor Domini super omnia se superposuit]]. [[Ecclus 25:15|Blessed is the man, to whom it is given to have the fear of God|Beatus cui datum est habere timorem Dei]]. [[Ecclus 40:28|The fear of the Lord is like a paradise of blessing|Timor Domini sicut paradisus benedictionis]] [the margin gives Ecclus. xi, 28; the words stand at Ecclus 40:28]. Now the fear of God is especially necessary to every Christian, for it preserves from vices, keeps in good things, and makes him who fears watchful lest he fall into the snares of the enemy. Again, we ought always to be watchful and trembling before God, for we know not whether we be worthy of love or hatred[[Eccles 9:1||]], that is, whether we be in charity and grace or not; and again because we know not what will finally be ours, whether everlasting damnation or perpetual salvation; and because we are so prone to every evil, and walk in the midst of snares.

paras.t: Præterea, ad conversandum tam timorate ac virtuose nos debet inducere, quod Unigenitus Dei, verus Deus, tanta pro nostra salute assumpsit, fecit ac pertulit. Ideo subditur : Scientes per fidem, non per naturalem rationem : de qua scientia dixit Job, Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum ; Martha quoque : Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die ; quod non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis, id est originalis infectionis seu vitiosæ informationis : quia parentes istorum quibus hæc scripta sunt, filios suos pessime docuerunt, ut scilicet idola colerent, quantum ad eos qui ex gentilibus nati erant. Sacerdotes quoque et Scribæ Judæorum, tradiderunt filiis suis ac subditis quædam divinæ legi contraria : quibus in Evangelio loquitur Christus, Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditionem vestram.
paras.en: Moreover, what ought to lead us to live so fearfully and virtuously is that the Only-begotten of God, true God, took on, did and endured such great things for our salvation. Therefore it is added: [[1:18|Knowing|Scientes]], by faith, not by natural reason; of which knowledge Job said: [[Job 19:25|I know that my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Scio quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]]; and Martha too: [[John 11:24|I know that he shall rise again, in the resurrection at the last day|Scio quia resurget in resurrectione in novissimo die]]; [[1:18|that you were not redeemed with corruptible things, as gold or silver, from your vain conversation of the tradition of your fathers|quod non corruptibilibus auro vel argento redempti estis de vana vestra conversatione paternæ traditionis]], that is, of original infection, or of vicious instruction: for the parents of those to whom this was written taught their sons most wickedly, namely to worship idols, as regards those born of the Gentiles. The priests and Scribes of the Jews also handed down to their sons and subjects certain things contrary to the divine law; to whom Christ says in the Gospel: [[Matt 15:6|you have made void the commandment of God for your tradition|Irritum fecistis mandatum Dei propter traditionem vestram]].

paras.t: Sed pretioso sanguine, quasi agni incontaminati et immaculati. Jesu Christi, id est passione et morte Filii Dei, qui est quasi agnus, quoniam innocentissimo agno assimilatur. De quo ait Joannes Baptista : Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi. Qui et per Jeremiam contestatur : Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam. Estque quasi agnus incontaminatus et immaculatus, propter immunitatem suam ab omni peccato, tam originali quam personali, tam mortali quam veniali. Christus quippe, quamvis pro originalis peccati deletione specialiter passus dicatur, sua tamen passione sanctissima pro cunctis totius humani generis peccatis, quantum in ipso est, satisfecit, juxta illud Isaiæ : Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum. Propter quod angelus dixit ad Joseph : Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum : ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum. —
paras.en: [[1:19|But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb unspotted and undefiled|Sed pretioso sanguine, quasi agni incontaminati et immaculati]], of Jesus Christ, that is, by the passion and death of the Son of God, who is as a lamb, since he is likened to a most innocent lamb. Of whom John the Baptist says: [[John 1:29|Behold the Lamb of God. Behold him who taketh away the sin of the world|Ecce Agnus Dei, qui tollit peccata mundi]]. Who also testifies through Jeremias: [[Jer 11:19|I was as a meek lamb, that is carried to be a victim|Ego quasi agnus mansuetus qui portatur ad victimam]]. And he is as a lamb unspotted and undefiled because of his freedom from all sin, original as well as personal, mortal as well as venial. For Christ, though he is said to have suffered especially for the blotting out of original sin, yet by his most holy passion made satisfaction, as far as lay in him, for all the sins of the whole human race, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 53:6|the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all|Dominus posuit in eo iniquitatem omnium nostrum]]. Wherefore the angel said to Joseph: [[Matt 1:21|thou shalt call his name Jesus. For he shall save his people from their sins|Vocabis nomen ejus Jesum : ipse enim salvum faciet populum suum a peccatis eorum]]. —

paras.t: Christi, inquam, præcogniti quidem ante constitutionem mundi, id est ab æterno ad hoc præordinati ac prævisi a Deo Patre, secundum naturam assumptam, ut per eum redimeretur genus humanum. Deus namque ab æterno decrevit per Christi passionem redimere mundum. Manifestati autem in novissimis temporibus propter vos, id est, propter vestram salutem, Christus in ultima mundi ætate per incarnationis mysterium apparuit in hoc mundo, juxta illud Baruch : Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est. Hoc est quod ait Joannes : Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis. Hinc ad Ephesios loquitur Paulus, dicendo : Deus elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem, in quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ejus. De his demum diebus novissimis loquitur Paulus : Nos sumus in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt.
paras.en: Of Christ, I say, [[1:20|Foreknown indeed before the foundation of the world|præcogniti quidem ante constitutionem mundi]], that is, from eternity foreordained and foreseen for this by God the Father, according to the nature assumed, that through him mankind should be redeemed. For God decreed from eternity to redeem the world by the passion of Christ. [[1:20|but manifested in the last times for you|Manifestati autem in novissimis temporibus propter vos]], that is, for your salvation, Christ appeared in this world in the last age of the world through the mystery of the Incarnation, according to that of Baruch: [[Bar 3:38|Afterwards he was seen upon earth, and conversed with men|Post hæc in terris visus est, et cum hominibus conversatus est]]. This is what John says: [[John 1:14|the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us|Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis]]. Hence Paul speaks to the Ephesians, saying: [[Eph 1:4|he chose us in him before the foundation of the world|elegit nos in Christo ante mundi constitutionem]], [[Eph 1:7|In whom we have redemption through his blood|in quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ejus]]. Of these last days, finally, Paul speaks: [[1 Cor 10:11|upon whom the ends of the world are come|in quos fines sæculorum devenerunt]].

paras.t: Qui per ipsum fideles estis in Deo, id est, virtute et merito passionis Christi, gratiam conversionis ac fidei consecuti estis a Deo, et hucusque fideles mansistis in eo. Meritum etenim Christi in sacramento Baptismi ac Pœnitentiæ applicatur hominibus : et quidquid virtutis et gratiæ eis confertur a Domino, per Christum et ejus passionem ac meritum ipsis donatur, in quantum per Christi mysteria Deus proposuit sibi reconciliare atque salvare genus humanum. Propter quod ad Ephesios habetur : Deus prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum in laudem gloriæ gratiæ suæ, in qua gratificavit nos in dilecto Filio suo. Vel, Per ipsum fideles estis in Deo, quoniam Christus suos misit discipulos ad aliorum conversionem ubique, et per Apostolos dedit hominibus legem salutis, quemadmodum apud Isaiam ait : Lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet. Idcirco ait Apostolus : In Christo, qui eratis longe, facti estis prope.
paras.en: [[1:21|Who through him are faithful in God|Qui per ipsum fideles estis in Deo]], that is, by the power and merit of Christ's passion you have obtained from God the grace of conversion and of faith, and have hitherto remained faithful in him. For the merit of Christ is applied to men in the sacrament of Baptism and of Penance; and whatever virtue and grace is conferred on them by the Lord is given them through Christ and his passion and merit, inasmuch as God purposed to reconcile mankind to himself and save it through the mysteries of Christ. Wherefore it is said to the Ephesians: [[Eph 1:5|predestinated us unto the adoption of children through Jesus Christ|prædestinavit nos in adoptionem filiorum per Jesum Christum]] [[Eph 1:6|Unto the praise of the glory of his grace, in which he hath graced us, in his beloved son|in laudem gloriæ gratiæ suæ, in qua gratificavit nos in dilecto Filio suo]]. Or: Through him you are faithful in God, because Christ sent his disciples everywhere for the conversion of others, and through the Apostles gave men the law of salvation, as he says in Isaias: [[Is 51:4|a law shall go forth from me, and my judgment shall rest to be a light of the nations|Lex a me exiet, et judicium meum in lucem populorum requiescet]]. Therefore the Apostle says: [[Eph 2:13|in Christ Jesus, you, who some time were afar off, are made nigh|In Christo, qui eratis longe, facti estis prope]].

paras.t: Qui suscitavit eum a mortuis tertia die. Quæ suscitatio toti superbenedictæ Trinitati, cujus opera ad extra sunt indivisa, adscribitur. Potest tamen Patri appropriari, quia divina virtute effecta est : virtus autem seu potentia Patri appropriatur. Imo Christus, secundum quod est Deus, suscitavit se ipsum ut homo est. Propter quod dixit : Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud. Et dedit ei gloriam sempiternam, id est perpetuam corporis glorificationem, accidentaleque præmium, et judiciariam potestatem, in resurrectione, ascensione, etc. Nam in beatifica Dei visione, anima Christi fuit, ab exordio suæ creationis et unionis cum Verbo, perfecta. Hinc Christus passione sua instante, oravit illud Joannis : Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum. Et ad Hebræos habetur : Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum. In Isaia quoque legitur : Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur. Ut fides vestra et spes esset in Domino, id est, firmiter crederetis in Deum, et speraretis in eo. Ex hoc enim quod Deus Christum ita glorificavit per resuscitationem, ascensionem, et Sancti Spiritus missionem, inducti sunt homines ad christianæ fidei ac spei susceptionem, credentes et sperantes se tandem merito Christi resuscitandos et plene glorificandos.
paras.en: [[1:21|who raised him up from the dead|qui suscitavit eum a mortuis]] on the third day. This raising is ascribed to the whole superblessed Trinity, whose works outwardly are undivided. Yet it can be appropriated to the Father, since it was wrought by divine power, and power or might is appropriated to the Father [that is, attributed to one Person by a fitting likeness, though common to all three]. Nay, Christ, as he is God, raised up himself as he is man. Wherefore he said: [[John 2:19|Destroy this temple; and in three days I will raise it up|Solvite templum hoc, et in tribus diebus excitabo illud]]. [[1:21|and hath given him glory|Et dedit ei gloriam]] everlasting, that is, the perpetual glorification of the body, and accidental reward, and judiciary power, in the resurrection, ascension, etc. For in the beatific vision of God the soul of Christ was perfect from the beginning of its creation and union with the Word. Hence Christ, as his passion drew near, prayed that prayer in John: [[John 17:1|said: the hour is come. Glorify thy Son, that thy Son|Pater, venit hora, clarifica Filium tuum]]. And it is said to the Hebrews: [[Heb 2:9|we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour|Videmus Jesum propter passionem mortis, gloria et honore coronatum]]. In Isaias too we read: [[Is 53:11|Because his soul hath laboured, he shall see and be filled|Pro eo quod laboravit anima ejus, videbit et saturabitur]]. [[1:21|that your faith and hope might be in God|Ut fides vestra et spes esset in Domino]], that is, that you might firmly believe in God and hope in him. For because God so glorified Christ by the resurrection, ascension and the sending of the Holy Ghost, men were led to receive the Christian faith and hope, believing and hoping that by the merit of Christ they would at last be raised up and fully glorified.

paras.t: Animas vestras castificantes, id est, cœlesti Sponso castas et puras exhibentes, in obedientia caritatis, id est obediendo divinis præceptis ex caritate, sine qua nulla est actio meritoria, Deoque grata. Omnis siquidem actus meritorius, est a caritate elicitive, ut actus qui immediate et directe procedunt ex caritate; aut imperative, ut actus aliarum virtutum quibus præcipit caritas. In fraternitatis amore, id est etiam in proximorum spirituali dilectione, sine qua nemo potest salvari. Ideo subditur : simplici ex corde, omni duplicitate et fictione exclusa, invicem diligite attentius, id est valde attente, quum dicat Salvator : In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem. Atque ut asserit Paulus : Qui diligit proximum, legem implevit. Porro de cordis simplicitate et duplicitate, dicta sunt multa super Canonicam Jacobi.
paras.en: [[1:22|Purifying your souls|Animas vestras castificantes]], that is, presenting them chaste and pure to the heavenly Bridegroom, [[1:22|in the obedience of charity|in obedientia caritatis]], that is, obeying the divine commandments out of charity, without which no action is meritorious and pleasing to God[[1 Cor 13:1||]]. For every meritorious act is from charity either elicitively, as the acts which proceed immediately and directly from charity, or imperatively, as the acts of the other virtues which charity commands [the scholastic distinction between acts produced by a virtue itself and acts of other virtues which it directs]. [[1:22|with a brotherly love|In fraternitatis amore]], that is, also in the spiritual love of our neighbours, without which no one can be saved. Therefore it is added: [[1:22|from a sincere heart|simplici ex corde]], all doubleness and pretence excluded, [[1:22|love one another earnestly|invicem diligite attentius]], that is, very attentively, since the Saviour says: [[John 13:35|By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another|In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]]. And as Paul asserts: [[Rom 13:8|he that loveth his neighbour hath fulfilled the law|Qui diligit proximum, legem implevit]]. Further, much was said of simplicity and doubleness of heart on the Canonical Epistle of James[[Jas 1:8||]].

paras.t: Omnis autem anima rationalis, aut est sponsa Dei per fidem ac caritatem, aut certe adultera diaboli per infidelitatem, seu quamcumque culpam mortalem. Ideo animas nostras castificare debemus modo prætacto, et omni virtute ornare, sanctis actibus decorare, incessabiliter, fructuose, timorate ac fervide conversari : præsertim quoniam tanti æstimavit nos Dominus Deus noster, quod propter nostram recuperandam salutem, nostram in unitate personæ assumpsit naturam, et in ea pro nobis tot et tanta fecit ac passus est. Nonne ex dignitate legati, magnitudo causæ pensatur? Quum ergo Unigenitum suum miserit Deus Pater legatum ad pacificandum nos sibi, quis magnitudinem causæ quam cum Deo habemus, excellentiamque beatitudinis ad quam sumus creati, concipere valeat aut effari? Hinc et aliam causam ob quam timorate vivere debeamus, dignissimus apostolici chori vertex subjungit.
paras.en: Every rational soul is either the bride of God through faith and charity, or else the adulteress of the devil through unbelief or any mortal fault. Therefore we must purify our souls in the manner touched on, adorn them with every virtue, beautify them with holy acts, and live unceasingly, fruitfully, fearfully and fervently: above all since the Lord our God esteemed us so highly that, to recover our salvation, he assumed our nature in the unity of his person, and in it did and suffered so many and so great things for us. Is not the greatness of a cause weighed by the dignity of the envoy? Since then God the Father sent his Only-begotten as envoy to make our peace with him, who can conceive or utter the greatness of the cause we have with God, and the excellence of the beatitude for which we were created? Hence the most worthy head of the apostolic choir adds another reason why we ought to live in fear.

paras.t: Renati non ex semine corruptibili, id est, Deum timere, invicemque attentius amare debetis, quia renati estis seu spiritualiter generati per emundationem a culpa, et susceptionem gratiæ ac virtutum, non ex materiali impuroque semine, sed incorruptibili, id est virtute cœlesti in sacramento Baptismatis operante, seu gratia spirituali et gratum faciente, quæ confert homini esse spirituale, supernaturale, deiforme, idoneum ad promerendum. per verbum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum, id est per Christum, de quo Joannes ait : Omnia per ipsum facta sunt. Nam Christus est qui principaliter interiusque baptizat, purgat, regenerat. Ipse quoque Baptismum instituit, et omnibus dari præcepit ; et ipse est Verbum increatum, æternum, unigenitum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum, videlicet Patris æterni, quemadmodum Petrus disseruit : Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi.
