Vel per verbum Dei vivi, intelligit formam verborum sacramentalium operantium in Baptismo, per quæ dispositive et suo modo causaliter fit regeneratio spiritualis : quoniam accedente verbo ad elementum, fit sacramentum. Unde et Paulus testatur, quod Christus dilexit Ecclesiam, mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ. De hac regeneratione dicta sunt plura super illud Jacobi, Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis. Unde Joannes ait : Dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, his qui credunt in nomine ejus, qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt.
paras.en: [[1:23|Being born again, not of corruptible seed|Renati non ex semine corruptibili]]: that is, you ought to fear God and love one another more earnestly, because you are born again, or spiritually begotten, through cleansing from fault and the receiving of grace and the virtues, not of material and impure seed, [[1:23|but incorruptible|sed incorruptibili]], that is, by the heavenly power working in the sacrament of Baptism, or by spiritual and sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], which gives man a spiritual, supernatural, godlike being, fit for meriting. [[1:23|by the word of God who liveth and remaineth for ever|per verbum Dei vivi et permanentis in æternum]], that is, through Christ, of whom John says: [[John 1:3|All things were made by him|Omnia per ipsum facta sunt]]. For it is Christ who principally and inwardly baptizes, cleanses, regenerates. He also instituted Baptism and commanded it to be given to all; and he is the uncreated, eternal Word, the only-begotten of the living God who remains for ever, namely of the eternal Father, as Peter declared: [[Matt 16:16|Thou art Christ, the Son of the living God|Tu es Christus Filius Dei vivi]]. Or by the word of the living God he means the form of the sacramental words working in Baptism, through which spiritual regeneration takes place dispositively and in its own way causally: for when the word is joined to the element, the sacrament is made. Hence Paul too testifies that [[Eph 5:25|Christ also loved the church|Christus dilexit Ecclesiam]], [[Eph 5:26|cleansing it by the laver of water in the word of life|mundans eam lavacro aquæ in verbo vitæ]]. Of this regeneration much was said on that of James: [[Jas 1:18|of his own will hath he begotten us by the word of truth|Voluntarie genuit nos verbo veritatis]]. Hence John says: [[John 1:12|he gave them power to be made the sons of God, to them that believe in his name|Dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, his qui credunt in nomine ejus]], [[John 1:13|Who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God|qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt]].

paras.t: Quia omnis caro fœnum. Tanquam dicat : Regeneratio spiritualis, ex carnali et corruptibili semine esse nequit : quoniam caro carnaleve semen, fœno assimilatur, idcirco ad spirituale et supernaturale esse non potest perducere, nec talis generationis semen exsistere. Unde ait Salvator : Quod natum est ex carne, caro est; et quod natum est ex spiritu, spiritus est. Et omnis gloria ejus, id est viror, vigor, voluptasque carnis, quasi flos fœni, id est, cito pertransit et deficit, sicut flos graminis. Exaruit fœnum, id est, gramen, postquam viruerit et excreverit, mox arescit, et flos ejus decidit. Sic caro in pueritia habet virorem, in adolescentia decorem, in juventute robur et florem, in senectute desiccationem, in morte corruptionem.
paras.en: [[1:24|For all flesh is as grass|Quia omnis caro fœnum]]. As though he said: Spiritual regeneration cannot come from carnal and corruptible seed; for flesh, or carnal seed, is likened to grass[[Is 40:6||]][[Ecclus 14:18||]], and therefore cannot bring one to spiritual and supernatural being, nor be the seed of such a generation. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 3:6|That which is born of the flesh is flesh: and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit|quod natum est ex spiritu, spiritus est]]. [[1:24|and all the glory thereof|Et omnis gloria ejus]], that is, the freshness, vigour and pleasure of the flesh, [[1:24|as the flower of grass|quasi flos fœni]], that is, quickly passes away and fails, like the flower of the grass. [[1:24|The grass is withered|Exaruit fœnum]], that is, the grass, after it has grown green and tall, soon dries up, [[1:24|and the flower thereof is fallen away|et flos ejus decidit]]. So the flesh has in childhood freshness, in youth comeliness, in manhood strength and bloom, in old age drying up, in death corruption.

paras.t: Verbum autem Domini manet in æternum. Quod primo verum est de Verbo increato Patris æterni. De quo scriptum est : In principio erat Verbum. De quo Damascenus intelligit illud in Psalmo, In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum permanet in cœlo. Secundo, verificatur de verbo creato, id est divinæ virtutis præcepto, effectu seu lege, qua cuncta subsistunt. De quo verbo cantatur : Ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, quæ faciunt verbum ejus ; et rursus, Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit. Tertio, de verbo sacræ Scripturæ, quod dicitur non transire, sed in æternum manere. Nam inviolabilis atque perpetua est veritas Scripturarum, quamvis verba vocalia sonando transeant, ac desinant esse, utpote de numero successivorum, quibus idem est esse et fieri. Ideo loquitur Christus : Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt. Quarto, de verbo sacramentali, quod manet in suo effectu. Nam character qui in Baptismo imprimitur, indelebilis perhibetur. Et gratia quæ ibi infunditur, ex se non habet ut corrumpatur, quamvis per accidens desinat esse in transgressore : quæ etiam gratia arrha vitæ æternæ vocatur. — Denique locus hic ex Isaia sumptus est, ubi habetur : Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri, etc.
paras.en: [[1:25|But the word of the Lord endureth for ever|Verbum autem Domini manet in æternum]]. This is true first of the uncreated Word of the eternal Father, of whom it is written: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. Of whom Damascene understands that in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:89|For ever, O Lord, thy word standeth firm in heaven|In æternum, Domine, verbum tuum permanet in cœlo]]. Secondly, it is verified of the created word, that is, the command, effect or law of the divine power by which all things subsist. Of which word it is sung: [[Ps 148:8|Fire, hail, snow, ice, stormy winds, which fulfil his word|Ignis, grando, nix, glacies, spiritus procellarum, quæ faciunt verbum ejus]]; and again: [[Ps 148:6|he hath made a decree, and it shall not pass away|Præceptum posuit, et non præteribit]]. Thirdly, of the word of Holy Scripture, which is said not to pass but to remain for ever. For the truth of the Scriptures is inviolable and perpetual, though the spoken words pass in the sounding and cease to be, being of the number of successive things, for which to be and to come to be are the same. Therefore Christ says: [[Luke 21:33|Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away|Cœlum et terra transibunt, verba autem mea non transibunt]]. Fourthly, of the sacramental word, which remains in its effect. For the character imprinted in Baptism is held to be indelible. And the grace infused there has not of itself that it should be corrupted, though accidentally it ceases to be in the transgressor; which grace is also called the pledge of eternal life. — Lastly, this passage is taken from Isaias, where we have: [[Is 40:6|All flesh is grass, and all the glory thereof as the flower of the field|Omnis caro fœnum, et omnis gloria ejus quasi flos agri]], etc.[[Is 40:8||]]

paras.t: Hoc autem est verbum quod evangelizatum est in vobis, id est, inter vos prædicatum per Christi Apostolos ceterosque discipulos : qui, Paulo testante, non prædicaverunt se ipsos, sed Jesum Christum, qui est Verbum æternum, et ejus doctrinam, præcepta ac sacramenta.
paras.en: [[1:25|And this is the word which by the gospel hath been preached unto you|Hoc autem est verbum quod evangelizatum est in vobis]], that is, preached among you by the Apostles of Christ and his other disciples, who, as Paul testifies, [[2 Cor 4:5|preach not ourselves, but Jesus Christ|non prædicaverunt se ipsos, sed Jesum Christum]], who is the eternal Word, and his doctrine, commandments and sacraments.

2.title: EXPLANATIO CAPITULI SECUNDI : DEPONENTES IGITUR OMNEM MALITIAM.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: Wherefore laying away all malice.

paras.t: Jam circa finem præcedentis capituli docuit princeps Apostolorum, quam pretiosi sint fideles per Christum redempti, quamque sublimiter regenerati: idcirco nunc plenius instruit eos, quam virtuose debeant conversari, ne tantis beneficiis sint ingrati: quia cui plus datum est, plus requiretur ab eo. Itaque ait: Deponentes igitur, id est, quum sitis taliter liberati atque renati, idcirco per contritionem seu anticipationem, removentes a cordibus vestris omnem malitiam, id est excogitatam ac deliberatam pravitatem, seu omnem habitum vitiosum consuetudinemque perversam; et omnem dolum in verbis et factis: siquidem virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus. Dolus namque caritati et justitiæ atque prudentiæ veræ contrariatur. Ideo Salomon protestatur: Vir versutus odiosus est. Et simulationes: simulatores enim et callidi provocant iram Dei; et invidias, id est rancores seu tristitias de prosperitatibus proximorum; et omnes detractiones: quæ sunt peccata mortifera. Quid autem sit detractio, et quot modis contingat, quam etiam enorme peccatum sit, et quomodo a detrahente sit fugiendum, dictum est supra, circa illud Jacobi: Nolite detrahere alterutrum, fratres mei.
paras.en: Towards the end of the preceding chapter the prince of the Apostles taught how precious are the faithful redeemed by Christ, and how sublimely they have been born again: therefore he now instructs them more fully how virtuously they ought to live, lest they be ungrateful for such great benefits: for [[Luke 12:48|unto whomsoever much is given, of him much shall be required|cui plus datum est, plus requiretur ab eo]]. So he says: [[2:1|Wherefore laying away|Deponentes igitur]], that is: since you have been thus set free and born again, therefore, by contrition or by forestalling [*anticipationem*: that is, by turning sin away before it takes hold, as contrition removes it after], removing from your hearts [[2:1|all malice|omnem malitiam]], that is, wickedness thought out and deliberate, or every vicious habit and perverse custom; [[2:1|and all guile|et omnem dolum]] in words and deeds: since [[Ps 5:7|The bloody and the deceitful man the Lord will abhor|virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus]]. For guile is contrary to charity and justice and true prudence. Therefore Solomon declares: [[Prov 14:17|the crafty man is hateful|Vir versutus odiosus est]]. [[2:1|and dissimulations|Et simulationes]]: for [[Job 36:13|Dissemblers and crafty men prove the wrath of God|simulatores enim et callidi provocant iram Dei]]; [[2:1|and envies|et invidias]], that is, rancours or sadness at the prosperity of our neighbours; [[2:1|and all detractions|et omnes detractiones]], which are deadly sins. But what detraction is, in how many ways it comes about, how grievous a sin it is, and how the detractor is to be shunned, has been said above, on that saying of James: [[Jas 4:11|Detract not one another, my brethren|Nolite detrahere alterutrum, fratres mei]].

paras.t: Sicut modo geniti infantes, id est instar parvulorum infantium statim natorum, quantum ad innocentiam, non quantum ad nescientiam: ideo subditur, rationabiles, id est discreti, et judicium rectæ rationis sequentes. Debemus enim infantibus assimilari, quantum ad bonas eorum proprietates, quæ sunt: nulli nocere, non concupiscere, non irasci, cito placari, non superbire. Propter quod ait Salvator: Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cælorum. Non autem debemus infantulis conformari, discretione carendo, instabiliter nos habendo, poma, pira, rebus pretiosissimis præferendo. Propter quod loquitur Paulus: Non simus parvuli fluctuantes; et denuo, Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote. Et in Proverbiis habetur: Usquequo parvuli diligitis infantiam? — Est ergo bona et virtuosa infantia, quæ vocatur infantia christianæ simplicitatis, quæ est innocentia atque sinceritas mentis. Ad quam beatissimus Petrus hoc loco redire nos admonet, ne alicui simus nocivi, imo cunctis pro posse proficui. Est quoque vituperanda infantia, quæ est asinina simplicitas, et imperitia periculosa. Unde apud Isaiam asseritur: Puer centum annorum morietur. Quid enim est puer centum annorum, nisi senex puerilis, insipiens et inconstans? Talis morietur morte æternalis miseriæ, sicut jam mortuus est morte culpæ.
paras.en: [[2:2|As newborn babes|Sicut modo geniti infantes]], that is, like little infants just born, as regards innocence, not as regards ignorance: therefore he adds, [[2:2|rational|rationabiles]] [Denis's text has *rationabiles*, agreeing with the infants: "being rational"; the Douay-Rheims, following *rationabile*, has "the rational milk"], that is, discerning, and following the judgement of right reason. For we ought to be made like infants as to their good properties, which are these: to hurt no one, not to covet, not to be angry, to be quickly appeased, not to be proud. Hence the Saviour says: [[Matt 18:3|unless you be converted, and become as little children, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|Nisi conversi fueritis, et efficiamini sicut parvuli, non intrabitis in regnum cælorum]]. But we ought not to be conformed to little infants by lacking discernment, by behaving unsteadily, by preferring apples and pears to the most precious things. Hence Paul says: [[Eph 4:14|we be no more children tossed to and fro|Non simus parvuli fluctuantes]]; and again, [[1 Cor 14:20|do not become children in sense. But in malice be children|Nolite pueri effici sensibus, sed malitia parvuli estote]]. And in Proverbs we have: [[Prov 1:22|O children, how long will you love childishness|Usquequo parvuli diligitis infantiam]]? [*infantiam*, "infancy", the word Denis goes on to use] There is, then, a good and virtuous infancy, which is called the infancy of Christian simplicity, that is, innocence and sincerity of mind. To this the most blessed Peter here admonishes us to return, so that we may be harmful to no one, but rather, as far as we can, profitable to all. There is also a blameworthy infancy, which is asinine simplicity and dangerous inexperience. Hence it is said in Isaias: [[Is 65:20|the child shall die a hundred years old|Puer centum annorum morietur]]. For what is a child of a hundred years but a childish old man, foolish and inconstant? Such a one will die the death of eternal misery, as he is already dead with the death of guilt.

paras.t: Itaque, Rationabiles sine dolo: maledictus enim dolosus, ut in Malachia scriptum est; lac concupiscite, id est, faciliora fidei documenta cum aviditate a doctoribus et prælatis vestris suscipite, ut paulatim proficiatis. Nam neophytis et noviter baptizatis, incipientibus et imperfectis, sunt primo faciliora fidei pabula exhibenda, quia difficiliorum mysteriorum nondum capaces sunt. Talibus quippe loquitur Paulus ad Hebræos: Indigetis ut doceamini quæ sunt elementa exordii sermonis Dei, et facti estis quibus lacte opus est, non solido cibo; et alibi: Tanquam parvulis in Christo lac vobis potum dedi, non escam; non enim poteratis accipere. Ut in eo crescatis in salutem, id est, per lactis hujus spirituale edulium, pertingatis ad charismata meliora, ad viciniora saluti, ad contemplationem cœlestium, atque purissimum Divinitatis amorem, ut de eorum sitis catalogo de quibus loquitur Paulus: Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos; et item, Perfectorum est solidus cibus, eorum qui pro consuetudine exercitatos habent sensus. Ideo Vas electionis hortatur: Æmulamini charismata meliora. Quum etenim in via Dei non proficere, sit deficere, debemus quotidie in gratia Dei virtutibusque proficere, bonis bona adjicere, et omne tempus vitæ præsentis fructuose expendere, quemadmodum ad Philippenses docet Apostolus: Caritas vestra semper magis ac magis abundet in scientia, ut probetis potiora, et sitis sinceri, et sine offensione.
paras.en: So then, [[2:2|rational|Rationabiles]], [[2:2|without guile|sine dolo]]: for [[Mal 1:14|Cursed is the deceitful man|maledictus enim dolosus]], as is written in Malachias; [[2:2|desire the rational milk|lac concupiscite]], that is, receive eagerly from your teachers and prelates the easier teachings of the faith, so that you may make progress little by little. For to neophytes and the newly baptized, to beginners and the imperfect, the easier food of the faith is to be offered first, since they are not yet capable of the harder mysteries. To such Paul speaks in Hebrews: [[Heb 5:12|you have need to be taught|Indigetis ut doceamini]] [[Heb 5:12|what are the first elements of the words of God: and you are become such as have need of milk and not of strong meat|quæ sunt elementa exordii sermonis Dei, et facti estis quibus lacte opus est, non solido cibo]]; and elsewhere: [[1 Cor 3:1|As unto little ones in Christ|Tanquam parvulis in Christo]] [[1 Cor 3:2|I gave you milk to drink, not meat: for you were not able|lac vobis potum dedi, non escam; non enim poteratis]] to receive it. [[2:2|that thereby you may grow unto salvation|Ut in eo crescatis in salutem]], that is, that through the spiritual food of this milk you may attain to the better gifts, to the things nearer to salvation, to the contemplation of heavenly things and the most pure love of the Godhead, so as to be in the number of those of whom Paul says: [[1 Cor 2:6|we speak wisdom among the perfect|Sapientiam loquimur inter perfectos]] [the margin gives 1 Cor. iii, 2; the words are 1 Cor 2:6]; and again, [[Heb 5:14|strong meat is for the perfect: for them who by custom have their senses exercised|Perfectorum est solidus cibus, eorum qui pro consuetudine exercitatos habent sensus]] [the margin gives Hebr. v, 13; the words are Heb 5:14]. Therefore the Vessel of election exhorts: [[1 Cor 12:31|be zealous for the better gifts|Æmulamini charismata meliora]]. For since on the way of God not to go forward is to fall back, we ought daily to go forward in the grace of God and in the virtues, to add good to good, and to spend all the time of this present life fruitfully, as the Apostle teaches the Philippians: [[Phil 1:9|your charity may more and more abound in knowledge|Caritas vestra semper magis ac magis abundet in scientia]], [[Phil 1:10|That you may approve the better things: that you may be sincere and without offence|ut probetis potiora, et sitis sinceri, et sine offensione]].

paras.t: Si tamen gustastis quam dulcis est Dominus, id est, tunc præfata documenta poteritis adimplere, si divinæ bonitatis suavitatem interiori gustastis palato. Quemadmodum enim homo diu esse non potest sine dilectione, ita nec sine delectatione, quia delectationem naturaliter appetit. Ideo, sicut qui spiritualis amoris expertes sunt, carnalibus affectibus detinentur; ita qui in Deo non delectantur, ejus dulcedinem degustando, carnales, viles et exteriores delectationes, delicias, consolationes requirunt. Nec potest carnalia vitia superare, spiritualibus inhærere, qui nihil divinæ consolationis ac interioris dulcedinis experitur. Porro, quam dulcis est Deus, aliqualiter in hac vita gustamus, ipsum per donum sapientiæ et fidem formatam cognoscendo seu contemplando, eumque sinceriter diligendo. In eo namque quod magis diligimus, magis delectari solemus. Ideo ait Psalmista: Memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum; et rursus, Delectare in Domino; itemque, Gustate et videte quoniam suavis est Dominus.
paras.en: [[2:3|If so be you have tasted that the Lord is sweet|Si tamen gustastis quam dulcis est Dominus]], that is: you will be able to fulfil the teachings given above if you have tasted with the inner palate the sweetness of the divine goodness. For as a man cannot be long without love, so neither without delight, since he naturally desires delight. Therefore, as those who have no share in spiritual love are held fast by carnal affections, so those who do not delight in God by tasting his sweetness seek carnal, base and outward delights, pleasures and consolations. Nor can he overcome carnal vices or cleave to spiritual things who experiences nothing of divine consolation and inner sweetness. Now, how sweet God is we taste in some measure in this life, by knowing or contemplating him through the gift of wisdom and formed faith [that is, faith given its form and life by charity], and by loving him sincerely. For in what we love more we are wont to delight more. Therefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 76:4|I remembered God, and was delighted|Memor fui Dei, et delectatus sum]]; and again, [[Ps 36:4|Delight in the Lord|Delectare in Domino]]; and likewise, [[Ps 33:9|O taste, and see that the Lord is sweet|Gustate et videte quoniam suavis est Dominus]].

paras.t: Sed posset quis interrogare, qualiter poterimus ad divinæ suavitatis gustum interim pertingere? Et respondendum, quod oportet successive proficere, coram Deo sollicite ambulare, carnalia oblectamenta despicere, operibus insistere virtuosis, et Deo ex caritate prompto corde servire, atque in omnibus Dei honorem optare, et zelum habere justitiæ, caritatis quoque et pietatis redundare visceribus; sicque ad copiosissimum ac frequentissimum divinæ suavitatis pertingemus saporem, et Dei amici et ei familiares efficiemur, ita quod cum Propheta ex sententia proferemus: Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine! Præterea, quoniam unusquisque in caritate exsistens, habet donum sapientiæ secundum aliquem gradum: potest quilibet talis aliqualiter degustare quam dulcis est Deus, in suis orationibus, meditationibus, affectionibusque ad eum, in bonis quoque operibus delectando, juxta illud, Servite Domino in lætitia. Deus etiam ex sua pietate immensa, frequenter gratiose prævenit homines, etiam imperfectos et incipientes, infundendo eis suæ bonitatis dulcem saporem, consolationem internam, jucundæ alacritatis perfusionem: sicque allicit eos sibi, et a terrenis carnalibusque avertit, quia gustato spiritu, desipit omnis caro. Conemur ergo ad prætactum divinæ dulcedinis saporem pertingere, ut carnalia cordialius atque facilius contemnamus, et spiritualibus ac divinis stabilius immoremur: imo pro gratia ista obtinenda Deum precemur. Propter quod subditur:
paras.en: But someone might ask how we shall be able, meanwhile, to attain to the taste of the divine sweetness. And the answer is that we must go forward step by step, walk solicitously before God[[Mich 6:8||]], despise carnal pleasures, apply ourselves to virtuous works, serve God out of charity with a ready heart, desire God's honour in all things, have a zeal for justice, and overflow with the bowels of charity and of loving-kindness; and so we shall attain to a most abundant and most frequent savour of the divine sweetness, and shall be made friends of God and his familiars, so that with the Prophet we shall say from the heart: [[Ps 30:20|O how great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord|Quam magna multitudo dulcedinis tuæ, Domine]]! [the margin gives Ps. xxxv, 9; the words are Ps 30:20] Moreover, since everyone who is in charity has the gift of wisdom in some degree, any such person can in some measure taste how sweet God is, in his prayers, meditations and affections towards him, and by delighting in good works also, according to that saying: [[Ps 99:2|serve ye the Lord with gladness|Servite Domino in lætitia]]. God also, out of his immense loving-kindness, often graciously goes before men, even the imperfect and beginners, pouring into them the sweet savour of his goodness, inward consolation, a flood of joyful eagerness: and so he draws them to himself and turns them away from earthly and carnal things, since once the spirit has been tasted, all flesh loses its savour. Let us strive, then, to attain to the savour of the divine sweetness spoken of, so that we may despise carnal things more heartily and more easily, and dwell more steadily on spiritual and divine things: nay, let us pray God for the obtaining of this grace. Hence there follows:

paras.t: Ad quem accedentes lapidem vivum, id est, Dominum Jesum Christum, qui est vivus lapis, spiritualiter accedentes, credendo et desiderando gratiosam adsistentiam ejus, et ejus illuminationem simpliciter postulando: juxta illud in Psalmo, Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini; et ad Hebræos, Adeamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus, ut misericordiam consequamur. Ad Deum quippe ubique præsentem, non passibus pedum, sed desideriis cordium actibusque virtutum, accedimus. Dicitur autem Christus lapis, ratione firmitatis et fundationis. Est etiam lapis vivus, quia secundum deitatem suam, est essentialiter vivens et vita, quemadmodum ait: Ego sum via, veritas et vita; itemque, Sicut Pater habet vitam in semetipso, sic dedit et Filio vitam habere in semetipso. Porro, secundum naturam assumptam, vivens est vita naturæ humanæ in optimo gradu, vita gratiæ in summo statu, vita gloriæ in excellentiæ termino possibili menti creatæ. Omnis quoque vita procedit ab ipso.
paras.en: [[2:4|Unto whom coming, as to a living stone|Ad quem accedentes lapidem vivum]], that is, to the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the living stone: coming spiritually, by believing in and desiring his gracious presence and help, and by simply asking for his enlightenment, according to that saying in the Psalm, [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini]]; and in Hebrews, [[Heb 4:16|Let us go therefore with confidence to the throne of grace: that we may obtain mercy|Adeamus cum fiducia ad thronum gratiæ ejus, ut misericordiam consequamur]]. For we come to God, who is present everywhere, not by the steps of our feet but by the desires of our hearts and the acts of the virtues. Now Christ is called a stone by reason of firmness and of foundation. He is also a living stone, because according to his Godhead he is essentially living, and life itself, as he says: [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|Ego sum via, veritas et vita]]; and likewise, [[John 5:26|as the Father hath life in himself, so he hath given to the Son also to have life in himself|Sicut Pater habet vitam in semetipso, sic dedit et Filio vitam habere in semetipso]]. Further, according to the nature assumed, he is living with the life of human nature in the best degree, the life of grace in the highest state, the life of glory at the utmost height of excellence possible to a created mind. And all life proceeds from him.

paras.t: Accedentes ergo ad lapidem istum, ab hominibus quidem reprobatum: primo, videlicet a Judæis incredulis, qui multas blasphemias evomuerunt in Christum, dicendo: Dæmonium habet, et insanit; homo vorax, potator vini; in Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia. Atque in passione, quando dixerunt: Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram, etc. Deinde reprobatus est a philosophis et tyrannis ac aliis perfidis. A Deo autem electum, secundum naturam assumptam, ut per eum salvaretur genus humanum. De quo per Isaiam loquitur Dominus: Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea. Imo Christus antonomastice vocatur Dei electus, utpote omnium electorum salvator et caput, qui Spiritum non ad mensuram accepit, cujus merito alii electionis consequuntur effectum. Et honorificatum. Christum enim Deus Pater multipliciter honorificavit, id est, honore dignum effecit ac demonstravit: dicendo ad eum, Tu es Filius meus dilectus; eumque omnibus præferendo; ejus quoque excellentiam per Prophetas atque Apostolos, et per miracula insinuando; in die quoque ascensionis eum super omnes cœlos ad suam dexteram collocando.
paras.en: Coming, then, to this stone, [[2:4|rejected indeed by men|ab hominibus quidem reprobatum]]: first, that is, by the unbelieving Jews, who spewed out many blasphemies against Christ, saying: [[John 10:20|He hath a devil and is mad|Dæmonium habet, et insanit]]; [[Matt 11:19|a man that is a glutton and a wine drinker|homo vorax, potator vini]]; [[Luke 11:15|He casteth out devils by Beelzebub, the prince of devils|in Beelzebub principe dæmoniorum ejicit dæmonia]]. And in the Passion, when they said: [[Luke 23:2|We have found this man perverting our nation|Hunc invenimus subvertentem gentem nostram]], etc. Afterwards he was rejected by philosophers and tyrants and other faithless men. [[2:4|but chosen|A Deo autem electum]] by God, according to the nature assumed, that through him the human race might be saved. Of him the Lord speaks through Isaias: [[Is 42:1|Behold my servant, I will uphold him: my elect, my soul delighteth in him|Ecce servus meus, suscipiam eum; electus meus, complacuit sibi in illo anima mea]]. Indeed Christ is called by antonomasia [that is, by a name used for the one who bears it pre-eminently] the elect of God, as being the saviour and head of all the elect, who received the Spirit not by measure, and by whose merit others obtain the effect of election. [[2:4|and made honourable|Et honorificatum]]. For God the Father has honoured Christ in many ways, that is, has made him and shown him worthy of honour: by saying to him, [[Mark 1:11|Thou art my beloved Son|Tu es Filius meus dilectus]]; by preferring him to all; by making known his excellence through the Prophets and Apostles and through miracles; and on the day of the Ascension by setting him above all the heavens at his right hand.

paras.t: Et ipsi, id est vos ipsi, fideles, tanquam lapides vivi, id est, per fidem et caritatem spiritualiter viventes ac firmi, qui tempore infidelitatis et impietatis fuistis tanquam lapides duri ac mortui: propter quod Dominus dixit per Ezechielem, Auferam a vobis cor lapideum, et dabo vobis cor carneum; superædificamini domos spirituales: id est, super Christum, qui est verum Ecclesiæ fundamentum, ædificamini in domos spirituales, ita ut sitis domus seu habitacula Christi, qui per dona gratiæ suæ demoretur in vobis. Christus namque per fidem, ut loquitur Paulus, habitat in nobis. Hoc est: ita habete vos, ut Deus per gratiarum suarum charismata, faciat vos domos seu habitacula sua; et vos ipsi, bene vivendo, facite vos habitacula Salvatoris. Imo, proficiendo in omni bono, magis ac magis sitis habitacula Dei. Christus enim est fundamentum Ecclesiæ, super quod unusquisque ædificare, fundare et stabilire se debet per fidem, spem, caritatem, aliasque virtutes et actus ac profectus earum. Propter quod ad Corinthios scriptum est: Unusquisque videat quomodo superædificet: fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus. Quemadmodum autem sunt multæ particulares Ecclesiæ, quæ omnes sunt una universalis Ecclesia militans, in sæculo peregrinans, ex omnibus populis constans; ita sunt multæ particulares spiritualesque domus, quæ omnes sunt una generalis domus ac civitas Dei. Unde ad Hebræos legitur: Moyses fidelis erat in tota domo Dei, tanquam famulus; Christus vero tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos. Atque ad Timotheum loquitur Paulus: Scias quomodo oportet conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi. Superædificamini quoque, modo prætacto, sacerdotium sanctum, id est in sacerdotes sanctos Dei, ita ut sitis spiritualiter Dei sacerdotes, offerre, id est ad offerendum, spirituales hostias, id est orationes et sanctas affectiones, eleemosynas, bonaque opera, non sacrificia legis carnalia, acceptabiles Deo, id est ei placentes, et meritorias vitæ æternæ, quia ex caritate procedunt: acceptabiles, inquam, per Jesum Christum, cujus virtute, gratia et merito superædificamur modo præhabito, et opera Deo placita operamur. Propter quod asserit Christus: Sicut palmes non potest ferre fructum a semetipso, nisi manserit in vite, sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis. Et rursus ibidem: Sine me, inquit, nihil potestis facere. Idcirco, in fine oblationum et orationum Ecclesiæ communiter dicitur: Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, etc., quia per ipsum nostræ oblationes et orationes sunt Deo gratæ sive acceptæ, et per ipsius perfectionem ac meritum suppletur imperfectum nostrum, dummodo illud humiliter recognoscamus, et actus nostros merito actuum passionisque Christi, capitis nostri, per fidem et caritatem sapientialiter uniamus, rogando Deum ut virtute ac merito conversationis passionisque Christi in sæculo isto, pie suscipiat actus nostros, et imperfecto nostro indulgeat.
paras.en: [[2:5|Be you also|Et ipsi]], that is, you yourselves, the faithful, [[2:5|as living stones|tanquam lapides vivi]], that is, living spiritually and firm through faith and charity, you who in the time of unbelief and ungodliness were like hard and dead stones: for which reason the Lord said through Ezechiel, I will take away from you [[Ezech 36:26|the stony heart|cor lapideum]], [[Ezech 36:26|and will give you a heart of flesh|et dabo vobis cor carneum]]; [[2:5|built up, a spiritual house|superædificamini domos spirituales]] [Denis's text has the plural, *domos spirituales*, "spiritual houses", as his gloss shows]: that is, be built upon Christ, who is the true foundation of the Church, into spiritual houses, so that you may be the houses or dwelling-places of Christ, who by the gifts of his grace abides in you. For Christ, as Paul says, dwells in us by faith[[Eph 3:17||]]. That is: so dispose yourselves that God, through the gifts of his graces, may make you his houses or dwelling-places; and you yourselves, by living well, make yourselves dwelling-places of the Saviour. Nay more, by going forward in every good, be more and more the dwelling-places of God. For Christ is the foundation of the Church, upon which each one ought to build, found and establish himself by faith, hope, charity and the other virtues, and their acts and growth. Hence it is written to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:10|let every man take heed how he buildeth thereupon|Unusquisque videat quomodo superædificet]]: [[1 Cor 3:11|For other foundation no man can lay, but that which is laid: which is Christ Jesus|fundamentum enim aliud nemo potest ponere, præter id quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus]]. And as there are many particular Churches, which are all one universal Church militant, on pilgrimage in this world, gathered from all peoples, so there are many particular and spiritual houses, which are all one general house and city of God. Hence we read in Hebrews: [[Heb 3:5|Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant|Moyses fidelis erat in tota domo Dei, tanquam famulus]] [Denis has *in tota domo Dei*, "in all the house of God"]; [[Heb 3:6|But Christ, as the Son in his own house: which house are we|Christus vero tanquam filius in domo sua, quæ domus sumus nos]]. And Paul says to Timothy: [[1 Tim 3:15|thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God|Scias quomodo oportet conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi]]. Be built up also, in the way just described, into [[2:5|a holy priesthood|sacerdotium sanctum]], that is, into holy priests of God, so that you may be spiritually priests of God, [[2:5|to offer up|offerre]], that is, for offering, [[2:5|spiritual sacrifices|spirituales hostias]], that is, prayers and holy affections, alms and good works, not the carnal sacrifices of the Law, [[2:5|acceptable to God|acceptabiles Deo]], that is, pleasing to him and meriting eternal life, since they proceed from charity: acceptable, I say, [[2:5|by Jesus Christ|per Jesum Christum]], by whose power, grace and merit we are built up in the way described, and work works pleasing to God. Hence Christ declares: [[John 15:4|As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, unless it abide in the vine, so neither can you, unless you abide in me|Sicut palmes non potest ferre fructum a semetipso, nisi manserit in vite, sic nec vos, nisi in me manseritis]]. And again in the same place: [[John 15:5|without me|Sine me]], he says, [[John 15:5|you can do nothing|nihil potestis facere]]. Therefore at the end of the offerings and prayers of the Church it is commonly said: Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc., because through him our offerings and prayers are pleasing or acceptable to God, and by his perfection and merit our imperfection is made up, provided that we humbly acknowledge it, and wisely unite our acts, through faith and charity, with the merit of the acts and the Passion of Christ our Head, asking God that, by the power and merit of Christ's life and Passion in this world, he may graciously receive our acts and pardon our imperfection.

paras.t: Denique, sicut Christus secundum quod homo, est templum Dei, et pontifex seu sacerdos ac hostia: templum, quia in eo habitat omnis plenitudo Divinitatis, secundum Paulum; sacerdos autem, quia ut dicitur ad Hebræos, Ipse per Spiritum Sanctum obtulit semetipsum immaculatum Deo: ita fideles sunt domus, templum et habitaculum Dei, in quantum per gratiam habitat in eisdem. Propter quod ad Corinthios dicitur: Nescitis quia templum Dei estis, et Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis? Sunt etiam sacerdotes et hostia Dei, in quantum se ipsos offerunt Deo. Unde ad Romanos scriptum est: Exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam sanctam, viventem, Deo placentem. Idcirco, quod dictum est, Sacerdotium sanctum, ad universos refertur fideles in caritate existentes, non ad eos dumtaxat qui sacramento Ordinis sacri sunt insigniti, ut quidam exponunt. Propter quod ait venerabilis Beda: Omnem Ecclesiam, sacerdotium sanctum appellat (quod nomen et officium sola domus Aaron in lege Moysis habuit), quoniam omnes summi Capitis membra sumus, et oleo sancto in Baptismo uncti consistimus.
paras.en: Lastly, as Christ, as man, is the temple of God, and the high priest or priest, and the victim: the temple, because [[Col 2:9|in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead|in eo habitat omnis plenitudo Divinitatis]], according to Paul; and priest, because, as is said in Hebrews, [[Heb 9:14|who by the Holy Ghost offered himself unspotted unto God|Ipse per Spiritum Sanctum obtulit semetipsum immaculatum Deo]]: so the faithful are the house, temple and dwelling-place of God, inasmuch as he dwells in them by grace. Hence it is said to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 3:16|Know you not that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?|Nescitis quia templum Dei estis, et Spiritus Dei habitat in vobis?]]? They are also priests and victims of God, inasmuch as they offer themselves to God. Hence it is written to the Romans: [[Rom 12:1|you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, pleasing unto God|Exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiam sanctam, viventem, Deo placentem]]. Therefore what is said, [[2:5|a holy priesthood|Sacerdotium sanctum]], refers to all the faithful who are in charity, not only to those who are marked with the sacrament of holy Order, as some explain it. Hence the Venerable Bede says: "He calls the whole Church a holy priesthood (a name and office which the house of Aaron alone had in the law of Moses)[[Ex 28:1||]], since we are all members of the supreme Head, and stand anointed with holy oil in Baptism."

paras.t: Propter quod continet Scriptura, id est, ob hoc quod Christus est lapis vivus, et quia ad ipsum debetis accedere, Deus per Isaiam testatur: Ecce ponam in Sion, id est in Ecclesia speculante cœlestia. Sion enim speculatio interpretatur. Unde ad Hebræos scribitur: Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis. Lapidem summum. Nam inter eos qui ratione soliditatis sive constantiæ, lapides appellantur, est Christus altissimus, qui est omnium rex Sanctorum. De quo in Daniele habetur, quod lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus, factus est mons magnus, et implevit universam superficiem terræ. Angularem. Christus vocatur lapis angularis, quia sicut in lapide angulari duo concurrunt et connectuntur parietes; sic in Christo duo populi convenerunt, unitique sunt, et unus populus per fidem et caritatem effectus. Propter quod loquitur Paulus: Christus est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum, ut duos condat in semetipso. Hinc in Zacharia de Christo prædictum est: Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus, et ædificabit templum Domino, et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos. Electum, secundum naturam assumptam, in omnium redemptorem. De quo in Canticis Sponsa fatetur: Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus. Pretiosum, imo dignissimum: quoniam Christus secundum quod Deus, est dignitatis prorsus incomparabilis et immensæ. Secundum assumptam vero humanitatem, ut Verbo æterno unitam, et omni gratiarum plenitudine perornatam, dignior est toto universo.
paras.en: [[2:6|Wherefore it is said in the scripture|Propter quod continet Scriptura]] [literally "the Scripture contains"], that is: because Christ is the living stone, and because you ought to come to him, God testifies through Isaias: [[2:6|Behold, I lay in Sion|Ecce ponam in Sion]][[Is 28:16||]] [Denis has *ponam*, "I will lay"], that is, in the Church, which beholds heavenly things. For *Sion* is interpreted "watch-tower" [*speculatio*: a looking-out, contemplation]. Hence it is written to the Hebrews: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis]]. [[2:6|a chief|Lapidem summum]] stone. For among those who are called stones by reason of their solidity or constancy, Christ is the highest, he who is the king of all the Saints. Of him we read in Daniel that [[Dan 2:34|a stone was cut out of a mountain without hands|lapis qui abscissus est de monte sine manibus]] [[Dan 2:35|became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth|factus est mons magnus, et implevit universam superficiem terræ]]. [[2:6|corner stone|Angularem]]. Christ is called the corner stone because, as in a corner stone two walls meet and are joined, so in Christ two peoples have come together and been united, and made one people through faith and charity. Hence Paul says: [[Eph 2:14|he is our peace, who hath made both one|Christus est pax nostra, qui fecit utraque unum]], [[Eph 2:15|that he might make the two in himself|ut duos condat in semetipso]] [the margin gives Eph. ii, 14, 17; the last words are Eph 2:15]. Hence it was foretold of Christ in Zacharias: [[Zach 6:12|BEHOLD A MAN, THE ORIENT IS HIS NAME|Ecce vir, Oriens nomen ejus]], [[Zach 6:12|and shall build a temple to the Lord|et ædificabit templum Domino]], [[Zach 6:13|and the counsel of peace shall be between them both|et consilium pacis erit inter duos illos]]. [[2:6|elect|Electum]], according to the nature assumed, to be the redeemer of all. Of him the Bride confesses in the Canticles: [[Cant 5:10|My beloved is white and ruddy, chosen out of thousands|Dilectus meus candidus et rubicundus, electus ex millibus]]. [[2:6|precious|Pretiosum]], nay most worthy: since Christ as God is of a dignity altogether incomparable and immense; and according to the humanity he assumed, as united to the eternal Word and adorned with all the fulness of graces, he is worthier than the whole universe.

paras.t: Et qui crediderit in eam fide formata, et perseveraverit usque in finem, non confundetur, quum fuerit divino tribunali oblatus, id est, non reprobabitur a Judice summo: quamvis in sæculo isto a pravis hominibus confundatur, vituperetur, dijudicetur, quemadmodum justi latentur in Psalmo: Posuisti nos in similitudinem gentibus, commotionem capitis in populis; tota die verecundia mea contra me est, et confusio faciei meæ cooperuit me. Hinc in alio fertur psalmo: Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini; et facies vestræ non confundentur. Hoc est quod de se ipso ait Salvator: Omnis qui videt Filium, et credit in eum, non morietur in æternum. Unde Joannes apostolus in sua hortatur Canonica: Manete in eo, ut quum apparuerit, habeamus fiduciam, et non confundamur ab eo in adventu ejus.
paras.en: [[2:6|And he that shall believe|Et qui crediderit]] in it [Denis reads *in eam*; the Vulgate has *in eum*, "in him"] with formed faith, and shall persevere unto the end, [[2:6|shall not be confounded|non confundetur]] when he is brought before the divine tribunal, that is, he shall not be rejected by the supreme Judge: although in this world he be put to confusion, reviled and condemned by wicked men, as the just say in the Psalm [the print has *latentur*, evidently a slip, perhaps for *fatentur*, "confess"]: [[Ps 43:15|Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: a shaking of the head among the people|Posuisti nos in similitudinem gentibus, commotionem capitis in populis]]; [[Ps 43:16|All the day long my shame is before me: and the confusion of my face hath covered me|tota die verecundia mea contra me est, et confusio faciei meæ cooperuit me]]. Hence it is said in another psalm: [[Ps 33:6|Come ye to him and be enlightened: and your faces shall not be confounded|Accedite ad eum, et illuminamini; et facies vestræ non confundentur]]. This is what the Saviour says of himself: [[John 6:40|every one who seeth the Son and believeth in him|Omnis qui videt Filium, et credit in eum]], [[John 11:26|shall not die for ever|non morietur in æternum]]. Hence John the Apostle exhorts in his Canonical Epistle: [[1 John 2:28|abide in him, that when he shall appear we may have confidence and not be confounded by him at his coming|Manete in eo, ut quum apparuerit, habeamus fiduciam, et non confundamur ab eo in adventu ejus]].

paras.t: Vobis igitur honor credentibus, quia in Christum credendo meremini ad cœlestem gloriam promoveri, atque a Deo in cœlestibus honorari, videlicet angelis sociari. Propterea asserit Christus: Si quis mihi ministraverit, honorificabit eum Pater meus. Nam honor debetur virtuti. Hinc perfidi, reprobi, et iniqui dicent in die judicii: Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam: quomodo ergo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est? ut in Sapientia inducitur. Non credentibus autem, id est ceteris in incredulitate sua durantibus, eisque nolentibus seu invitis, lapis quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, id est Christus, quem doctores et sacerdotes Judæorum plebem communem instruentes, et eam per hoc spiritualiter ædificantes, verbis et factis persequebantur (juxta illud Jeremiæ: Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt. Non est ipse), hic factus est in caput anguli, id est principium angulare, in quo duo populi convenerunt, sicut expositum est.
paras.en: [[2:7|To you therefore that believe, he is honour|Vobis igitur honor credentibus]]: because by believing in Christ you merit to be raised to heavenly glory and to be honoured by God in heaven, that is, to be made the companions of the angels. Therefore Christ declares: [[John 12:26|If any man minister to me, him will my Father honour|Si quis mihi ministraverit, honorificabit eum Pater meus]]. For honour is due to virtue. Hence the faithless, the reprobate and the wicked will say on the day of judgment: [[Wis 5:4|We fools esteemed their life madness|Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam]]: [[Wis 5:5|how they are numbered among the children of God, and their lot is among the saints|quomodo ergo computati sunt inter filios Dei, et inter Sanctos sors illorum est?]]? as they are brought in speaking in Wisdom. [[2:7|but to them that believe not|Non credentibus autem]], that is, to the rest, who persist in their unbelief, and against their will or in spite of themselves, [[2:7|the stone which the builders rejected|lapis quem reprobaverunt ædificantes]], that is, Christ, whom the doctors and priests of the Jews, who instructed the common people and so built them up spiritually, persecuted by words and deeds (according to that of Jeremias: [[Jer 5:12|They have denied the Lord, and said, It is not he|Negaverunt Dominum, et dixerunt. Non est ipse]]), [[2:7|the same is made the head of the corner|hic factus est in caput anguli]], that is, the corner foundation [Latin *principium angulare*, the corner principle or beginning], in which the two peoples came together, as has been explained.

paras.t: Et lapis offensionis et petra scandali factus est Christus, non directe, neque ex culpa sua, sed occasionaliter, his qui offendunt verbo, id est obstinatis Judæis, et cunctis incredulis, blasphemantibus Christum, nec credunt in quo positi sunt, id est, Scripturis legis et Prophetarum, secundum verum earum intellectum non credunt, quum tamen facti essent et positi ad credendum: quia Scriptura legis et Prophetarum fuit dispositiva ad Christum, et data, ut per eam Judæi præpararentur ad Christi fidem ac legem. Propter quod dicitur ad Galatas: Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo. His excæcatis Judæis Christus in Evangelio ait: Si crederetis Moysi, crederetis forsitan et mihi; de me enim ille scripsit. Et rursus: Scrutamini Scripturas, quia illæ sunt quæ testimonium perhibent de me. De quibus et per Danielem prædictum est: Non erit ejus (scilicet Christi) populus qui eum negaturus est. Per Isaiam quoque: Quis cæcus, nisi servus meus? et quis surdus, nisi ad quem nuntios meos misi? His itaque fuit Christus occasionaliter lapis offensionis, petraque scandali: nam ex sua perversitate offenderunt et impegerunt in Christum; atque ex ejus beneficiis, informationibus, increpationibus, deteriores et damnabiliores effecti sunt. Hinc sæpe in Evangelio leguntur scandalizati in Christo. Et in Joanne loquitur Christus: Si non venissem, et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent; nunc autem excusationem non habent de peccato suo.
paras.en: [[2:8|And a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal|Et lapis offensionis et petra scandali]] Christ became, not directly, nor through any fault of his, but occasionally [that is, as the occasion of their fall, not its cause], [[2:8|to them who stumble at the word|his qui offendunt verbo]], that is, to the obstinate Jews and all unbelievers, who blaspheme Christ, [[2:8|neither do believe, whereunto also they are set|nec credunt in quo positi sunt]]: that is, they do not believe the Scriptures of the law and the Prophets according to their true sense, though they had been made and set for believing; for the Scripture of the law and the Prophets was a preparation for Christ, and was given so that by it the Jews might be made ready for the faith and law of Christ. For which reason it is said to the Galatians: [[Gal 3:24|the law was our pedagogue in Christ|Lex pædagogus noster fuit in Christo]]. To these blinded Jews Christ says in the Gospel: [[John 5:46|if you did believe Moses, you would perhaps believe me also: for he wrote of me|Si crederetis Moysi, crederetis forsitan et mihi; de me enim ille scripsit]]. And again: [[John 5:39|Search the scriptures|Scrutamini Scripturas]], for [[John 5:39|the same are they that give testimony of me|quia illæ sunt quæ testimonium perhibent de me]]. Of them it was also foretold through Daniel: [[Dan 9:26|the people that shall deny him shall not be his|Non erit ejus (scilicet Christi) populus qui eum negaturus est]] (*his*, that is, Christ's). And through Isaias too: [[Is 42:19|Who is blind, but my servant? or deaf, but he to whom I have sent my messengers?|Quis cæcus, nisi servus meus? et quis surdus, nisi ad quem nuntios meos misi?]] To these, then, Christ was occasionally a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal: for by their own perversity they stumbled and struck against Christ, and from his benefits, his teachings and his rebukes they were made worse and more damnable. Hence we often read in the Gospel that they were scandalized in Christ[[Matt 13:57||]][[Matt 15:12||]]. And in John Christ says: [[John 15:22|If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin: but now they have no excuse for their sin|Si non venissem, et locutus eis fuissem, peccatum non haberent; nunc autem excusationem non habent de peccato suo]].

paras.t: Denique scandalum active, directe et proprie dictum, est semper peccatum, quum sit dictum vel factum minus rectum, alteri præbens occasionem ruinæ. Et sic Christus non fuit lapis offensionis, petrave scandali. Scandalum vero occasionaliter et indirecte, et quasi passive dictum, non est peccatum. Sic enim scandalum est, aliquod verbum aut opus bonum, ex quo ex propria abusione et deordinatione aliqui sumunt occasionem ruinæ ac peccant. Sicque Christus fuit lapis offensionis et petra scandali. Propter quod loquitur Paulus: Nos autem prædicamus Christum, Judæis quidem scandalum, gentibus autem stultitiam. Unde in libro Sapientiæ dicunt iniqui: Gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum, quia dissimilis est aliis vita illius. — Postremo, quod dictum est, Lapis offensionis et petra scandali, sumptum est ex Isaia, ubi habetur: Dominum sanctificate, et erit vobis in sanctificationem: in lapidem autem offensionis et petram scandali, duabus domibus Israel.
paras.en: Further, scandal taken actively, directly and properly is always a sin, since it is a word or deed less than right that gives another an occasion of falling [this is the scholastic definition of scandal]. And in this way Christ was not a stone of stumbling or a rock of scandal. But scandal taken occasionally and indirectly, and as it were passively, is not a sin. For scandal in this sense is some good word or work from which some, through their own misuse and disorder, take occasion of falling and sin. And in this way Christ was a stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal. For which reason Paul says: [[1 Cor 1:23|But we preach Christ|Nos autem prædicamus Christum]], [[1 Cor 1:23|unto the Jews indeed a stumblingblock, and unto the Gentiles foolishness|Judæis quidem scandalum, gentibus autem stultitiam]]. Hence in the book of Wisdom the wicked say: [[Wis 2:15|He is grievous unto us, even to behold: for his life is not like other men's|Gravis est nobis etiam ad videndum, quia dissimilis est aliis vita illius]]. Lastly, what is said, [[2:8|A stone of stumbling and a rock of scandal|Lapis offensionis et petra scandali]], is taken from Isaias, where we read: [[Is 8:13|Sanctify the Lord|Dominum sanctificate]], [[Is 8:14|And he shall be a sanctification to you. But for a stone of stumbling, and for a rock of offence to the two houses of Israel|et erit vobis in sanctificationem: in lapidem autem offensionis et petram scandali, duabus domibus Israel]].

paras.t: Reprobatis itaque Judæis incredulis, ponit princeps Apostolorum, fidelium Judæorum omniumque in Christum credentium, sublime præconium. Vos autem ad Christum conversi, estis genus electum, id est ad specialem gratiam præ ceteris a Deo præordinatum, utpote ad fidem catholicam, ceterasque virtutes, et ecclesiastica sacramenta, vocatum atque perductum. Non enim omnium est fides. Et dici potest de vobis illud ex Psalmo: Non fecit taliter omni nationi. Regale sacerdotium, id est sacerdotes regii seu regales, videlicet Christo summo regi ac sacerdoti assimilati et incorporati, ac pertinentes ad eum. Siquidem, ut dictum est, quemadmodum Christus homo, est templum Dei, sacerdos ac hostia: sic Christianus fidelis, est templum, sacerdos ac hostia Dei. Et quoniam summi Regis sacerdos est, et sacerdotium ejus ad regnum ordinatur cœleste, merito regalis sacerdos vocatur. Denique omnes fideles reges dicuntur, se ipsos per rationem regendo, passiones ac vitia superando. Sacerdotes quoque dicuntur, hostiam laudis, sacrificium orationis, munera eleemosynarum, et cetera spiritualia exercitia, virtuosaque opera Domino offerendo. Propterea in Apocalypsi patentur: Christus fecit nos regnum et sacerdotes Deo et Patri suo. Gens sancta, id est divino cultui deputata, in Baptismo mundata, virtutibus decorata. Quemadmodum autem lex Christi, est lex totius perfectionis; sic veri Christiani, Christi legem splendide observantes, recte præ cunctis populis sancta gens appellantur. Et tales præcipue erant Christiani in primitiva Ecclesia, quos Paulus in suis epistolis tam frequenter nominat sanctos. Populus acquisitionis, id est Christi sanguine de manu inimicorum humanæ salutis ereptus, liberatus, adeptus. Venit enim Filius hominis quærere et salvare quod perierat, ut ipsemet in Evangelio protestatur. Qui iterum ait: Congratulamini mihi, quia inveni ovem quam perdideram. Unde in Actibus loquitur Paulus: Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo vos posuit Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo; et ad Hebræos, Non sumus subtractionis filii in perditionem, sed fidei in acquisitionem animæ.
paras.en: Having thus set aside the unbelieving Jews, the prince of the Apostles sets out a lofty praise of the faithful Jews and of all who believe in Christ. [[2:9|But you|Vos autem]], converted to Christ, [[2:9|are a chosen generation|estis genus electum]], that is, foreordained by God above the rest to a special grace, called and brought, that is, to the catholic faith, to the other virtues and to the sacraments of the Church. For [[2 Thess 3:2|all men have not faith|Non enim omnium est fides]] [the margin gives II Thess. iii, without the verse]. And that of the Psalm may be said of you: [[Ps 147:9|He hath not done in like manner to every nation|Non fecit taliter omni nationi]] [the margin's book is unreadable; its verse number, 20, follows the Hebrew count, in which this Psalm continues Ps 146]. [[2:9|a kingly priesthood|Regale sacerdotium]], that is, royal or kingly priests, made like to Christ, the supreme king and priest, incorporated into him and belonging to him. For, as has been said, just as Christ as man is the temple of God, priest and victim, so the faithful Christian is the temple, priest and victim of God. And since he is the priest of the supreme King, and his priesthood is ordered to the heavenly kingdom, he is rightly called a kingly priest. Further, all the faithful are called kings, in that they rule themselves by reason and overcome their passions and vices; and priests too, in that they offer to the Lord the victim of praise, the sacrifice of prayer, the gifts of almsgiving, and their other spiritual exercises and virtuous works. Therefore it is made plain in the Apocalypse: Christ [[Apoc 1:6|hath made us a kingdom, and priests to God and his Father|fecit nos regnum et sacerdotes Deo et Patri suo]]. [[2:9|a holy nation|Gens sancta]], that is, set apart for the worship of God, cleansed in Baptism, adorned with virtues. And just as the law of Christ is the law of all perfection, so true Christians, who keep the law of Christ splendidly, are rightly called a holy nation above all peoples. And such above all were the Christians in the early Church, whom Paul so often calls saints in his epistles[[Rom 1:7||]][[Rom 12:13||]][[1 Cor 1:2||]][[Eph 1:1||]] [the margin gives Rom. i, 7; xii, 13; 1 Cor. xiv, 1; Ephes. i, 1, etc.; 1 Cor 14:1 does not speak of the saints, so 1 Cor 1:2 is marked here]. [[2:9|a purchased people|Populus acquisitionis]] [literally, a people of acquisition], that is, snatched out of the hand of the enemies of man's salvation by the blood of Christ, set free and won. For [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit enim Filius hominis quærere et salvare quod perierat]], as he himself declares in the Gospel [the margin gives Luke xv, 10; the words are Luke 19:10]. And again he says: [[Luke 15:6|Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost?|Congratulamini mihi, quia inveni ovem quam perdideram]] Hence Paul says in the Acts: [[Acts 20:28|Take heed to yourselves and to the whole flock, wherein the Holy Ghost hath placed you bishops, to rule the Church of God which he hath purchased with his own blood|Attendite vobis et universo gregi, in quo vos posuit Spiritus Sanctus episcopos, regere Ecclesiam Dei, quam acquisivit sanguine suo]] [*acquisivit*, the word behind *acquisitionis*]; and to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:39|we are not the children of withdrawing unto perdition, but of faith to the saving of the soul|Non sumus subtractionis filii in perditionem, sed fidei in acquisitionem animæ]] [in the Latin, *in acquisitionem animæ*, to the acquiring of the soul].

paras.t: Inductum autem præconium ait Moyses ad populum Judæorum: quod multo excellentius competit plebi Christianorum, cui majora gratiarum charismata sunt collata. Quidam exponunt hæc specialiter de sacerdotibus evangelicæ legis: qui dicuntur genus electum, id est ad consecrationem corporis et sanguinis Christi, præ ceteris consecrati et assumpti; quibus valde singularis dignitas, supernaturalis potestas, admirabilis ordo, collata sunt; ad quos ecclesiasticorum sacramentorum confectio et administratio pertinent. Quum enim in Numeris Moyses dicat Levitis, Num parum vobis est, quod separavit vos Dominus a populo, et junxit sibi, ut serviretis ei in cultu tabernaculi? multo magis istud sacerdotibus Christi poterit dici. Sacerdotibus quoque et Levitis veteris Testamenti Ezechias rex ait secundo Paralipomenon libro: Nolite negligere; vos elegit Dominus ut stetis coram eo, et ministretis ei, colatisque eum, et cremetis ei incensum. Multo ergo sublimius, constituti in sacris Ordinibus evangelicæ legis, dici possunt genus electum. Qui etiam sunt regale sacerdotium, id est sacerdotes Christi regis altissimi; et gens sancta, quia ad eos præcipue pertinet vita perfecta, conversatio exemplaris. — Quod autem sequitur, ad utramque expositionem congrue applicatur.
paras.en: Now the praise brought in here is what Moses spoke to the people of the Jews[[Ex 19:6||]]; but it befits far more excellently the Christian people, on whom greater gifts of grace have been bestowed. Some expound these words especially of the priests of the law of the Gospel, who are called [[2:9|a chosen generation|genus electum]], that is, consecrated and taken up above the rest for the consecration of the body and blood of Christ; on whom a most singular dignity, a supernatural power and a wonderful order have been bestowed; and to whom belong the making and the administering of the sacraments of the Church. For since in Numbers Moses says to the Levites: [[Num 16:9|Is it a small thing unto you, that the God of Israel hath spared you from all the people, and joined you to himself, that you should serve him in the service of the tabernacle|Num parum vobis est, quod separavit vos Dominus a populo, et junxit sibi, ut serviretis ei in cultu tabernaculi?]]? this can be said far more of the priests of Christ. To the priests and Levites of the Old Testament also, king Ezechias says in the second book of Paralipomenon: [[2 Par 29:11|be not negligent: the Lord hath chosen you to stand before him, and to minister to him, and to worship him, and to burn incense to him|Nolite negligere; vos elegit Dominus ut stetis coram eo, et ministretis ei, colatisque eum, et cremetis ei incensum]]. Far more sublimely, then, can those set in holy Orders in the law of the Gospel be called [[2:9|a chosen generation|genus electum]]. They are also [[2:9|a kingly priesthood|regale sacerdotium]], that is, priests of Christ the most high king; and [[2:9|a holy nation|gens sancta]], since a perfect life and an exemplary conversation belong to them above all. What follows, however, fits both expositions well.

paras.t: Ut virtutes annuntietis ejus, id est, Dei omnipotentis caritatem, pietatem, sapientiam, justitiam, potestatem laudetis ac prædicetis, seu invicem enarretis, qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum, id est, de caligine ignorantiæ et peccati atque perfidiæ, ad splendorem fidei lucemque gratiæ ac virtutum vos transtulit: imo ad lumen gloriæ, et ad increati luminis sui (quod ipse est, qui lucem habitat inaccessibilem) beatificam visionem invitavit. Hanc enim Christus suis promittit fidelibus, qui ad Patrem suum ait: Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam; et alibi, Manifestabo ei me ipsum.
paras.en: [[2:9|that you may declare his virtues|Ut virtutes annuntietis ejus]], that is, that you may praise and proclaim, or tell to one another, the charity, mercy, wisdom, justice and power of almighty God, [[2:9|who hath called you out of darkness into his marvelous light|qui de tenebris vos vocavit in admirabile lumen suum]]: that is, who has brought you over from the gloom of ignorance, sin and unbelief to the splendour of faith and the light of grace and of the virtues; nay more, has invited you to the light of glory and to the beatific vision of his uncreated light (which he himself is, who [[1 Tim 6:16|inhabiteth light inaccessible|lucem habitat inaccessibilem]]). For Christ promises this to his faithful, when he says to his Father: [[John 17:24|Father, I will that where I am, they also whom thou hast given me may be with me: that they may see my glory|Pater, quos dedisti mihi, volo ut ubi ego sum, et illi sint mecum, ut videant claritatem meam]]; and elsewhere: I [[John 14:21|will manifest myself to him|Manifestabo ei me ipsum]].

paras.t: Qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem populus Dei: id est, ante conversionem vestram ad fidei veritatem, fuistis non populus Dei, secundum præsentem justitiam, quia non pertinuistis ad Deum per caritatem et gratiam ac debitam subjectionem, sed aversi fuistis ab eo, et ratione peccati attinebatis diabolo, cujus membra ac ministri fuistis. Verumtamen per prædestinationem æternam omnes electi, quantumcumque ad tempus iniqui sunt, semper sunt populus Dei. Sed et reprobi, omnesque communiter homines, sunt populus Dei per creationem ac providentiam. Nam et de talibus loquitur Deus apud Isaiam: Populus meus non intellexit. In Actibus quoque Paulus de bonis et malis communiter protestatur: Genus Dei sumus. Fideles autem et justi, sunt specialiter populus Dei, juxta illud Psalmi, Nos autem populus ejus, et oves pascuæ ejus: quia per caritatem et gratiam Deo conjuncti et subditi sunt.
paras.en: [[2:10|Who in times past were not a people: but are now the people of God|Qui aliquando non populus, nunc autem populus Dei]]: that is, before your conversion to the truth of the faith you were not the people of God as regards present justice, since you did not belong to God by charity and grace and due subjection, but were turned away from him and, by reason of sin, belonged to the devil, whose members and servants you were. Yet by eternal predestination all the elect, however wicked they may be for a time, are always the people of God. And the reprobate too, and all men alike, are the people of God by creation and providence. For of such also God says in Isaias: [[Is 1:3|my people hath not understood|Populus meus non intellexit]]. In the Acts, too, Paul declares of good and bad alike: [[Acts 17:28|we are also his offspring|Genus Dei sumus]] [Denis's wording: We are the offspring of God]. But the faithful and the just are in a special way the people of God, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 99:3|We are his people and the sheep of his pasture|Nos autem populus ejus, et oves pascuæ ejus]] [no reference in the margin; Ps 94:7 is close too]; for by charity and grace they are joined and subject to God.

paras.t: Qui non consecuti misericordiam, id est, ante conversionem vestram nondum fuistis adepti misericordiam hanc magnam, qua facti estis membra et milites Christi. Nullus tamen in isto sæculo expers est penitus misericordiæ Dei. Nam et infideles ac impii, misericorditer tolerantur et exspectantur a Deo, ut convertantur; atque per angelos eorum custodes retrahuntur a diversis periculis et peccatis; quotidianis quoque beneficiis Dei utuntur. Propter quod Salvator ait: Altissimus benignus est super ingratos et malos; et alibi, Solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos, et pluit super justos et injustos. Damnati etiam in inferno, aliquid misericordiæ sortiuntur, quia citra condignum torquentur. Imo in omni opere Dei misericordia et justitia ejus relucent, juxta quod scriptum est: Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas. Electi tamen specialiter dicuntur misericordiam consequi, unde et vasa misericordiæ appellantur; non autem iniqui et reprobi, qui vasa iræ vocantur. Ideo subditur: nunc autem misericordiam consecuti, id est gratiose a Deo vocati, et conversi. Donum enim Dei est, non ex operibus.
paras.en: [[2:10|Who had not obtained mercy|Qui non consecuti misericordiam]]: that is, before your conversion you had not yet gained this great mercy, by which you have been made members and soldiers of Christ. Yet no one in this world is wholly without a share in God's mercy. For even unbelievers and the ungodly are mercifully borne with and waited for by God, that they may be converted; they are drawn back from various dangers and sins by their guardian angels; and they enjoy God's daily benefits. For which reason the Saviour says: The Most High [[Luke 6:35|is kind to the unthankful and to the evil|benignus est super ingratos et malos]]; and elsewhere: he [[Matt 5:45|maketh his sun to rise upon the good, and bad, and raineth upon the just and the unjust|Solem suum oriri facit super bonos et malos, et pluit super justos et injustos]]. Even the damned in hell receive some share of mercy, since they are tormented less than they deserve. Nay, in every work of God his mercy and justice shine out, as it is written: [[Ps 24:10|All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth|Universæ viæ Domini misericordia et veritas]]. Yet it is the elect in a special way who are said to obtain mercy, and so they are called [[Rom 9:23|vessels of mercy|vasa misericordiæ]]; not so the wicked and the reprobate, who are called [[Rom 9:22|vessels of wrath|vasa iræ]]. Therefore he adds: [[2:10|but now have obtained mercy|nunc autem misericordiam consecuti]], that is, called by God's grace, and converted. For [[Eph 2:8|it is the gift of God|Donum enim Dei est]], [[Eph 2:9|Not of works|non ex operibus]].

paras.t: Istud ex Osee sumptum est, ubi Dominus ait: Vocabo non plebem meam, plebem meam; et non misericordiam consecutam, misericordiam consecutam. Quod et Paulus ad Romanos de gentilium conversione allegat, quia de ea ad litteram loquitur Osee propheta. Inter eos vero quibus beatissimus princeps Apostolorum hanc scripsit epistolam, aliqui erant ex gentilitate conversi, ad quos istud specialiter applicatur.
paras.en: This is taken from Osee[[Osee 2:24||]], where the Lord says: [[Rom 9:25|I will call that which was not my people, my people|Vocabo non plebem meam, plebem meam]]; and [[Rom 9:25|her that had not obtained mercy; one that hath obtained mercy|non misericordiam consecutam, misericordiam consecutam]] [Denis gives the words as Paul cites them in Rom 9:25; in Osee 2:24 the Douay-Rheims reads: I will say to that which is not my people: Thou art my people]. Paul too adduces this to the Romans[[Rom 9:25||]], of the conversion of the Gentiles, since the prophet Osee speaks of that in the literal sense. And among those to whom the most blessed prince of the Apostles wrote this epistle, some had been converted from the Gentiles, and to them this is applied in a special way.

paras.t: Præterea, quoniam tanto spiritualior debet esse Christifidelium vita, quanto præclariora gratiarum charismata eis sunt condonata, ideo recte subjungit et hortatur nos summus Apostolus: Carissimi, obsecro vos. Hoc suæ fuit profundissimæ humilitatis, quod eos tam affectuose rogavit quod cum auctoritate præcipere potuit. Sic et Paulus Philemoni scribens: Fiduciam, inquit, habens imperandi tibi quod ad rem pertinet, propter caritatem magis obsecro. Multi namque facilius vincuntur, flectuntur, alliciuntur humilitate et pietate, quam rigore et severitate. Obsecratio quoque est potissima species orationis. Est enim obsecratio, per sacra rogatio. Fitque interdum per sacrum increatum, ut quum ait Propheta, Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu, propter bonitatem tuam, Domine; et Paulus ad Romanos, Obsecro vos, fratres, per misericordiam Dei: interdum per sacrum creatum, ut quum dicimus, Per passionem et crucem tuam libera nos, Domine. Et fieri potest pariter per utrumque, ut si dicamus: Propter infinitam pietatem tuam miserere mei, Deus, per omne meritum Christi. Fit autem per sacrum increatum, tanquam per principale et superdignissimum inductivum: per sacrum autem creatum, tanquam per inductivum et medium secundarium, instrumentale ac meritorium. Et quando fit per sacrum utrumque simul, tunc est efficacissima prorsus oratio.
paras.en: Further, since the life of Christ's faithful ought to be the more spiritual the more splendid the gifts of grace bestowed on them, the chief Apostle rightly adds this and exhorts us: [[2:11|Dearly beloved, I beseech you|Carissimi, obsecro vos]]. It was a mark of his very deep humility that he asked them so affectionately for what he could have commanded with authority. So too Paul, writing to Philemon: Having [[Philem 1:8|confidence|Fiduciam]], he says, [[Philem 1:8|to command thee that which is to the purpose|habens imperandi tibi quod ad rem pertinet]], [[Philem 1:9|For charity sake I rather beseech|propter caritatem magis obsecro]]. For many are more easily won over, swayed and drawn by humility and kindness than by rigour and severity. Beseeching is also the most powerful kind of prayer. For beseeching is asking by holy things [Latin *obsecratio*, entreaty, is here taken from *ob sacra*, “by holy things”]. Sometimes it is made by something holy and uncreated, as when the Prophet says: [[Ps 24:7|According to thy mercy remember thou me: for thy goodness' sake, O Lord|Secundum misericordiam tuam memento mei tu, propter bonitatem tuam, Domine]]; and Paul to the Romans: [[Rom 12:1|I beseech you|Obsecro vos]], [[Rom 12:1|brethren, by the mercy of God|fratres, per misericordiam Dei]]; sometimes by something holy and created, as when we say: By thy passion and cross deliver us, O Lord. And it can be made by both together, as if we say: For thy infinite mercy have mercy on me, O God, through all the merit of Christ. When it is made by something holy and uncreated, it is made as by the principal and most surpassingly worthy motive; when by something holy and created, as by a secondary motive and means, instrumental and meritorious. And when it is made by both holy things together, then it is altogether the most effective prayer.

paras.t: Itaque, Obsecro vos, tanquam advenas et peregrinos. Fideles dicuntur advenæ, in quantum degunt in terra non sua. Sunt enim in mundo isto quasi in exsilio; et peregrini, quia ad cœlestem patriam gradiuntur, prout in exordio expositionis hujus epistolæ dictum est. Abstinere vos a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam, id est a concupiscentiis pravis animam impugnantibus: quia inclinant ad illicita, quæ sunt animarum saluti contraria, juxta illud ad Galatas: Caro concupiscit adversus spiritum, et spiritus adversus carnem: hæc enim sibi invicem adversantur. Unde, quo lex Christi divinior spiritualiorque consistit, eo carnalia desideria, eorumque opera magis dedecent Christianos: quia brutis assimilant hominem, rationem prorsus obtenebrant, et turpitudo maxima est in eis. Pariunt quoque fastidium divinorum, et spiritualia bona faciunt homini esse insipida. Idcirco in Ecclesiastico legitur: Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt etiam sapientes. Et in Osee habetur: Fornicatio et vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor.
paras.en: So, then: [[2:11|I beseech you, as strangers and pilgrims|Obsecro vos, tanquam advenas et peregrinos]]. The faithful are called strangers inasmuch as they live in a land not their own; for they are in this world as in exile; and pilgrims, because they are journeying to the heavenly fatherland, as was said at the beginning of this exposition of the epistle. [[2:11|to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|Abstinere vos a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]], that is, from the evil concupiscences that assail the soul: for they incline to unlawful things, which are contrary to the salvation of souls, according to that to the Galatians: [[Gal 5:17|the flesh lusteth against the spirit: and the spirit against the flesh: For these are contrary one to another|Caro concupiscit adversus spiritum, et spiritus adversus carnem: hæc enim sibi invicem adversantur]]. Hence the more divine and spiritual the law of Christ is, the more unbecoming to Christians are carnal desires and their works: for they make man like the brutes, darken the reason altogether, and there is the greatest foulness in them. They also breed a distaste for divine things, and make spiritual goods tasteless to a man. That is why we read in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 19:2|Wine and women make wise men fall off|Vinum et mulieres apostatare faciunt etiam sapientes]] [Latin *apostatare*, to fall away, apostatize]. And in Osee we have: [[Osee 4:11|Fornication, and wine, and drunkenness, take away the understanding|Fornicatio et vinum et ebrietas auferunt cor]] [Latin *cor*, the heart].

paras.t: Sed posset quis dicere: Si a carnalibus desideriis abstinere oportet, ergo a desiderio ciborum et potuum erit cavendum, nec licebit conjugatis se invicem cognoscere, quum hoc sine carnalibus desideriis fieri nequeat. Et respondendum, quod carnalia desideria proprie nominantur concupiscentiæ inordinatæ, seu irrefrenatæ appetitiones sensualitatis. Desideria vero gustus et tactus sub rationis ordine posita, licita sunt, et quodammodo spiritualia, utpote moderata, atque ad debitum spiritualemque finem relata. Ideo hortatur Paulus: Curam carnis ne feceritis in desideriis. Et denuo: Debitores, inquit, sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus: si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini: si autem spiritu facta carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis.
paras.en: But someone might say: If we must refrain from carnal desires, then we shall have to beware of the desire for food and drink, and married people will not be allowed to know one another, since this cannot be done without carnal desires. The answer is that carnal desires, properly so called, are disordered concupiscences, or the unbridled cravings of sensuality. But the desires of taste and touch, when placed under the order of reason, are lawful, and in a manner spiritual, since they are moderate and directed to a due and spiritual end. Therefore Paul exhorts: [[Rom 13:14|make not provision for the flesh in its concupiscences|Curam carnis ne feceritis in desideriis]]. And again: [[Rom 8:12|we are debtors|Debitores]], he says, [[Rom 8:12|not to the flesh to live according to the flesh|sumus non carni, ut secundum carnem vivamus]]: [[Rom 8:13|For if you live according to the flesh, you shall die: but if by the Spirit you mortify the deeds of the flesh, you shall live|si enim secundum carnem vixeritis, moriemini: si autem spiritu facta carnis mortificaveritis, vivetis]].

paras.t: Carnales igitur affectus, et eorum effectus, oscula et amplexus, ludos, jocos, cachinnos, voluptates, vanitates, vilesque consolationes despiciamus, neque in rebus sæculi hujus mentem figamus, sed ad patriam felicitatis æternæ totis properemus præcordiis: quemadmodum peregrini non quærunt in via morari aut deliciari, sed ad patriam properant et adspirant. Istud ad omnem pertinet Christianum, quum dicat Salvator: Væ vobis divitibus, qui habetis consolationem vestram; væ vobis qui saturati estis, quia esurietis; væ vobis qui ridetis nunc, quia plorabitis. Unde ad Galatas inducitur: Qui autem sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis. Itaque in cibo, potu, somno, vestitu, et ceteris ad corpus spectantibus, non superfluitatem aut voluptatem, sed necessitatem quæramus, quemadmodum Vas electionis hortatur: Habentes alimenta et quibus tegamur, his contenti simus. Propter quod Sapiens deprecatur: Tribue tantum victui meo necessaria. Quum igitur regali ac sacerdotali simus nomine insigniti, vitiorum jugo subjici dedignemur, ne a condonata gratiæ nobilitate, promissæque gloriæ sublimitate degeneremus.
